chapters.title: Make Me a Sanctuary
chapters.html:
Exodus 25

The Contribution

1And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them take up a contribution for Me. From every man whose heart moves him you shall take My contribution.

3And this is the contribution you shall take from them: gold and silver and bronze,

4and blue and purple and crimson, and fine linen and goats' hair,

5and rams' skins dyed red, and fine leather, and acacia wood,

6oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense,

7onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.

8And let them make Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them.

9According to all that I show you — the pattern of the dwelling and the pattern of all its furnishings — so you shall make it.

The Ark

10And they shall make an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits its length, and a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height.

11And you shall overlay it with pure gold — inside and outside you shall overlay it — and you shall make on it a molding of gold all around.

12And you shall cast for it four rings of gold and put them on its four feet: two rings on its one side and two rings on its other side.

13And you shall make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

14And you shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark by them.

15The poles shall stay in the rings of the ark. They shall not be taken out of it.

16And you shall put into the ark the Testimony that I will give you.

17And you shall make a cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits its length and a cubit and a half its width.

18And you shall make two cherubim of gold — hammered work you shall make them — at the two ends of the cover.

19And make one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end. Of one piece with the cover you shall make the cherubim, at its two ends.

20And the cherubim shall spread their wings upward, sheltering the cover with their wings, and their faces one toward the other. Toward the cover shall the faces of the cherubim be.

21And you shall put the cover on the ark from above, and into the ark you shall put the Testimony that I will give you.

22And I will meet with you there, and I will speak with you from above the cover, from between the two cherubim that are on the ark of the Testimony — everything that I command you for the sons of Israel.

The Table

23And you shall make a table of acacia wood, two cubits its length and a cubit its width and a cubit and a half its height.

24And you shall overlay it with pure gold, and make for it a molding of gold all around.

25And you shall make for it a rim a handbreadth wide all around, and make a molding of gold for its rim all around.

26And you shall make for it four rings of gold, and put the rings on the four corners that are at its four legs.

27The rings shall be close to the rim, as holders for the poles to carry the table.

28And you shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and the table shall be carried by them.

29And you shall make its dishes and its pans and its jars and its bowls, for pouring out drink offerings. Of pure gold you shall make them.

30And you shall set on the table the bread of the Presence, before Me always.

The Lampstand

31And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold. Hammered work the lampstand shall be made — its base and its shaft, its cups, its bulbs and its blossoms shall be of one piece with it.

32And six branches shall come out of its sides: three branches of the lampstand from its one side and three branches of the lampstand from its other side.

33Three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the one branch, a bulb and a blossom, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the next branch, a bulb and a blossom — so for the six branches coming out of the lampstand.

34And on the lampstand itself, four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its bulbs and its blossoms.

35And a bulb under the first two branches of one piece with it, and a bulb under the next two branches of one piece with it, and a bulb under the next two branches of one piece with it — for the six branches coming out of the lampstand.

36Their bulbs and their branches shall be of one piece with it, all of it one hammered work of pure gold.

37And you shall make its seven lamps, and its lamps shall be set up to give light in front of it.

38And its tongs and its trays shall be of pure gold.

39Of a talent of pure gold it shall be made, with all these furnishings.

40And see, and make them by their pattern, which you are being shown on the mountain."

Notes

  • v2 "a contribution… whose heart moves him" — terumah, from rum, to lift: a portion lifted off a larger amount and set aside. And the qualification is asher yiddvennu libbo, whose heart makes him willing. The sanctuary is funded by nothing but what people choose to give, and the list that follows is the exact inventory of what a nation carried out of Egypt.

  • v8 "and I will dwell among them" — not in it. The building is commanded and then the purpose is stated in the plural, about the people: be-tokham, in their midst. The verb is shakhan, to settle down and stay, which gives the sanctuary its Hebrew name in the next verse — mishkan, the dwelling — and much later gives Judaism the word shekhinah for God's settled presence.

  • vv9, 40 "the pattern" — tavnit, from banah, to build: a model, the thing a builder works from. The instruction opens and closes on it, and v40 says Moses is being shown it on the mountain. The Greek renders it typos, and Hebrews quotes that verse from the Greek almost word for word — see that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain (8:5) — to argue that the whole sanctuary was a copy of something else.

  • v17 "a cover" — kapporet, from the root kipper, to cover over and so to atone; the Day of Atonement is Yom Kippur from the same three letters. The Greek calls it the hilastērion, the place where atonement is made, and that is the word Paul uses of Jesus in Romans 3:25. English "mercy seat" comes down from Tyndale and is a translation of Luther's Gnadenstuhl, not of the Hebrew, which says only cover.

  • vv18–20 "two cherubim… hammered work" — beaten out of the same sheet as the cover, so they are not attached to it; they are it. The last time this canon mentioned cherubim, they were posted at the east of the garden with a turning sword to guard the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24). Here they are made objects again, wings spread over the lid of a box, facing each other and looking down.

  • v22 "and I will meet with you there" — ve-no'adti lekha sham, from the root behind mo'ed, an appointed meeting. This is the sentence the ark exists for. Everything before it is joinery and gold leaf; this is what the container is for — a place with an address, where God says He will be found and will speak, from the empty space between two golden figures.

  • v30 "the bread of the Presence" — lechem panim, literally bread of the face. The same noun that carries God's face everywhere else in Exodus: they shall not appear before My face empty-handed (23:15), no one can see My face and live (33:20). Twelve loaves sit on a table in the dark, permanently, in front of a face.

  • vv31–36 the lampstand is a tree — the pieces are named as botany: a yarekh (base, the same noun as the loin), a qaneh (shaft, also a reed or stalk), qanim (branches), kaftorim (bulbs or calyxes), and perachim (blossoms). Six branches come off a central stem, and the cups are meshuqqadim, almond-blossomed, three times over. What stands in the sanctuary giving light is a stylized almond tree in gold.

  • v33 "almond" — shaqed, and the tree is the first to flower in that country, before its own leaves are out. The word is one letter from shoqed, watching, staying awake, and Jeremiah's call turns on exactly that: he sees maqqel shaqed, an almond branch, and God answers shoqed ani al devari la-asoto — I am watching over My word to do it (Jeremiah 1:11–12). The tree that wakes first is the tree the language uses for staying awake.

  • v31 "hammered work" — miqshah, the lampstand and the cherubim both. Not cast in a mold and not assembled from parts: beaten out of a single mass of metal, so that no seam exists anywhere in either object. Verse 39 gives the budget for it as a talent of gold — roughly the weight of a grown man's load, all of it one piece.

chapters.title: The Dwelling
chapters.html:
Exodus 26

The Ten Curtains

1"And the dwelling you shall make of ten curtains of fine twisted linen, and blue and purple and crimson. With cherubim, the work of a designer, you shall make them.

2The length of one curtain, twenty-eight cubits, and the width of one curtain, four cubits. One measure for all the curtains.

3Five of the curtains shall be joined to one another, and five curtains joined to one another.

4And you shall make loops of blue on the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set, and do the same on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.

5Fifty loops you shall make on the one curtain, and fifty loops you shall make on the edge of the curtain that is in the second set, the loops facing one another.

6And you shall make fifty clasps of gold, and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, and the dwelling shall be one.

The Tent Over It

7And you shall make curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the dwelling. Eleven curtains you shall make of them.

8The length of one curtain, thirty cubits, and the width of one curtain, four cubits. One measure for the eleven curtains.

9And you shall join five of the curtains by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves, and you shall fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.

10And you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second set.

11And you shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and put the clasps into the loops and join the tent, and it shall be one.

12And the overhang left over from the curtains of the tent — the half curtain that is left over — shall hang over the back of the dwelling.

13And the cubit on this side and the cubit on that side, of what is left over in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the dwelling, on this side and on that, to cover it.

14And you shall make a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above that.

The Frames

15And you shall make the frames for the dwelling of acacia wood, standing upright.

16Ten cubits the length of a frame, and a cubit and a half the width of each frame.

17Two tenons for each frame, fitted to one another. So you shall do for all the frames of the dwelling.

18And you shall make the frames for the dwelling: twenty frames for the south side, facing south.

19And forty sockets of silver you shall make under the twenty frames — two sockets under one frame for its two tenons, and two sockets under the next frame for its two tenons.

20And for the second side of the dwelling, the north side, twenty frames,

21and their forty sockets of silver — two sockets under one frame and two sockets under the next frame.

22And for the rear of the dwelling, toward the west, you shall make six frames.

23And two frames you shall make for the corners of the dwelling at the rear.

24And they shall be paired below, and together they shall be flush at the top, at the first ring. So it shall be for both of them; they shall be for the two corners.

25And there shall be eight frames, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets — two sockets under one frame and two sockets under the next frame.

26And you shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the frames of the one side of the dwelling,

27and five bars for the frames of the second side of the dwelling, and five bars for the frames of the side of the dwelling at the rear, toward the west.

28And the middle bar, in the middle of the frames, shall run through from end to end.

29And the frames you shall overlay with gold, and their rings you shall make of gold, as holders for the bars. And you shall overlay the bars with gold.

30And you shall raise up the dwelling according to its ruling, which you were shown on the mountain.

The Veil and the Screen

31And you shall make a veil of blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen. The work of a designer shall make it, with cherubim.

32And you shall hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold, their hooks of gold, on four sockets of silver.

33And you shall hang the veil under the clasps, and bring in there, inside the veil, the ark of the Testimony. And the veil shall divide for you between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

34And you shall put the cover on the ark of the Testimony in the Holy of Holies.

35And you shall set the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table, on the south side of the dwelling; and the table you shall put on the north side.

36And you shall make a screen for the entrance of the tent, of blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.

37And you shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia and overlay them with gold, their hooks of gold, and cast for them five sockets of bronze."

Notes

  • vv1, 31, 36 two grades of craft — the Hebrew names the workmanship each time and does not use the same word twice by accident. The inner curtains and the veil are ma'aseh choshev, the work of a designer — from chashav, to think, calculate, devise — and both carry cherubim. The screen at the outer door is ma'aseh roqem, the work of an embroiderer, and has no figures on it. The further in, the more the fabric is credited to thinking rather than needlework.

  • vv1, 7 two structures, two names — mishkan, the dwelling, is the inner layer of ten linen curtains; ohel, the tent, is the eleven goats'-hair curtains thrown over it. English usually calls the whole thing the tabernacle and loses the distinction, but the chapter keeps them apart line by line: gold clasps for the dwelling, bronze clasps for the tent.

  • v3 "joined to one another" — the Hebrew is ishah el achotah, a woman to her sister, and it says it four times in this chapter about curtains, loops and tenons. It is simply how Hebrew says each to the next when the noun is grammatically feminine; the matching masculine idiom is ish el achiv, a man to his brother. No woman and no sister is meant, which is exactly why a literal English rendering would say something the Hebrew does not.

  • vv5, 24 "facing one another… paired below" — the whole structure is described by how its parts meet: loops opposite loops, tenons fitted, frames doubled at the corner, one bar running the full length. The sanctuary is specified almost entirely as a set of joints.

  • v14 "fine leather" — techashim, and nobody knows what animal this is. Dolphin, dugong, badger, antelope and a word for a color or a tanning process have all been proposed, from the Greek onward. It is the outermost layer, the one exposed to weather and the only part of the structure anyone outside would see, and the word for it cannot be recovered.

  • v15 "standing upright" — omdim, a participle hung on the end of a sentence about timber. Acacia is a desert tree, scrubby and thorny; the wood the whole frame is cut from is the toughest thing that grows where these people are. The verse says the boards stand, and the same root is what a person does before God.

  • v24 "flush at the top" — tammim, and it is the word the book uses for a person who is whole: Noah was tamim in his generations (Genesis 6:9), Abraham was told be tamim (17:1), Jacob was an ish tam (25:27). Here it is a carpentry term for two boards meeting cleanly with no gap. The moral word and the joinery word are the same word, and the joinery is the plain sense.

  • v30 "according to its ruling" — ke-mishpato, the same noun that opened the law code five chapters back: these are the rulings you shall set before them (21:1). A judgment and a set of assembly instructions are the same kind of thing in this language — the settled, correct way a matter goes.

  • v31 "a veil… with cherubim" — parokhet, which the Greek renders katapetasma. That is the word in Matthew 27:51: and here — the veil of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom. And the figures woven into it are the third appearance of cherubim in three chapters of this canon: posted at the garden gate in Genesis 3:24, beaten into the lid of the ark in 25:18, and now embroidered across the one door nobody may pass. Wherever a boundary is absolute, this book puts cherubim on it.

  • v33 "the Holy of Holies" — qodesh ha-qodashim, and Hebrew has no word for most. To make a superlative it repeats the noun in the plural and hangs it off itself: holy of the holies, the same construction as king of kings and song of songs. The innermost room is named by a grammatical trick for saying the most.

speech.text: Exodus 26
The Ten Curtains
"And the dwelling you shall make of ten curtains of fine twisted linen, and blue and purple and crimson. With cherubim, the work of a designer, you shall make them.
The length of one curtain, twenty-eight cubits, and the width of one curtain, four cubits. One measure for all the curtains.
Five of the curtains shall be joined to one another, and five curtains joined to one another.
And you shall make loops of blue on the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set, and do the same on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.
Fifty loops you shall make on the one curtain, and fifty loops you shall make on the edge of the curtain that is in the second set, the loops facing one another.
And you shall make fifty clasps of gold, and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, and the dwelling shall be one.
The Tent Over It
And you shall make curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the dwelling. Eleven curtains you shall make of them.
The length of one curtain, thirty cubits, and the width of one curtain, four cubits. One measure for the eleven curtains.
And you shall join five of the curtains by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves, and you shall fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
And you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
And you shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and put the clasps into the loops and join the tent, and it shall be one.
And the overhang left over from the curtains of the tent — the half curtain that is left over — shall hang over the back of the dwelling.

And the cubit on this side and the cubit on that side, of what is left over in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the dwelling, on this side and on that, to cover it.
And you shall make a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above that.
The Frames
And you shall make the frames for the dwelling of acacia wood, standing upright.
Ten cubits the length of a frame, and a cubit and a half the width of each frame.
Two tenons for each frame, fitted to one another. So you shall do for all the frames of the dwelling.
And you shall make the frames for the dwelling: twenty frames for the south side, facing south.
And forty sockets of silver you shall make under the twenty frames — two sockets under one frame for its two tenons, and two sockets under the next frame for its two tenons.
And for the second side of the dwelling, the north side, twenty frames,
and their forty sockets of silver — two sockets under one frame and two sockets under the next frame.
And for the rear of the dwelling, toward the west, you shall make six frames.
And two frames you shall make for the corners of the dwelling at the rear.
And they shall be paired below, and together they shall be flush at the top, at the first ring. So it shall be for both of them; they shall be for the two corners.
And there shall be eight frames, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets — two sockets under one frame and two sockets under the next frame.
And you shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the frames of the one side of the dwelling,
and five bars for the frames of the second side of the dwelling, and five bars for the frames of the side of the dwelling at the rear, toward the west.
And the middle bar, in the middle of the frames, shall run through from end to end.
And the frames you shall overlay with gold, and their rings you shall make of gold, as holders for the bars. And you shall overlay the bars with gold.
And you shall raise up the dwelling according to its ruling, which you were shown on the mountain.
The Veil and the Screen
And you shall make a veil of blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen. The work of a designer shall make it, with cherubim.
And you shall hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold, their hooks of gold, on four sockets of silver.
And you shall hang the veil under the clasps, and bring in there, inside the veil, the ark of the Testimony. And the veil shall divide for you between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.
And you shall put the cover on the ark of the Testimony in the Holy of Holies.
And you shall set the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table, on the south side of the dwelling; and the table you shall put on the north side.
And you shall make a screen for the entrance of the tent, of blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
And you shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia and overlay them with gold, their hooks of gold, and cast for them five sockets of bronze."

chapters.title: The Altar and the Court
chapters.html:
Exodus 27

The Altar

1"And you shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide — the altar shall be square — and three cubits its height.

2And you shall make its horns on its four corners. Its horns shall be of one piece with it, and you shall overlay it with bronze.

3And you shall make its pots for clearing its ashes, and its shovels and its basins and its forks and its fire pans. All its vessels you shall make of bronze.

4And you shall make for it a grating, a network of bronze, and on the network you shall make four bronze rings at its four corners.

5And you shall set it under the ledge of the altar, below, so that the network reaches halfway up the altar.

6And you shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.

7And its poles shall be put into the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.

8Hollow, of boards, you shall make it. As He showed you on the mountain, so they shall make it.

The Court

9And you shall make the court of the dwelling. For the south side, facing south, hangings for the court of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long for the one side,

10and its twenty pillars and their twenty sockets of bronze, the hooks of the pillars and their bands of silver.

11And so for the north side, in its length, hangings a hundred long, and its twenty pillars and their twenty sockets of bronze, the hooks of the pillars and their bands of silver.

12And for the width of the court on the west side, hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten and their sockets ten.

13And the width of the court on the east side, facing the sunrise, fifty cubits.

14And fifteen cubits of hangings for the one shoulder, their pillars three and their sockets three.

15And for the other shoulder, fifteen of hangings, their pillars three and their sockets three.

16And for the gate of the court, a screen of twenty cubits, of blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer; their pillars four and their sockets four.

17All the pillars of the court all around shall be banded with silver, their hooks of silver and their sockets of bronze.

18The length of the court, a hundred cubits, and the width fifty by fifty, and the height five cubits, of fine twisted linen; and their sockets of bronze.

19All the vessels of the dwelling, in all its service, and all its pegs and all the pegs of the court, shall be bronze.

The Lamp

20And you — you shall command the sons of Israel, and let them bring you clear oil of beaten olives for the light, to set up a lamp continually.

21In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is over the Testimony, Aaron and his sons shall set it in order from evening until morning before the LORD. A lasting statute for their generations, from the sons of Israel."

Notes

  • v2 "its horns… of one piece with it" — qarnot, horns, projecting from the four corners and beaten out of the same block, not fixed on. Nothing here says what they are for, but the law already assumed it: you shall take him from My altar to die (21:14) only makes sense if a man could run to the altar and expect to be safe. Centuries later Adonijah does exactly that — he rose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar (1 Kings 1:50). A frightened man's first move was to grab these, and the chapter that describes them never explains why.

  • v3 "its pots for clearing its ashes" — one Hebrew word, ledashno, built from deshen, the fat ash left by a burnt offering. The verb made from the noun means to take the noun away: to de-ash. English does this too — to dust a shelf is to remove dust, to bone a fish is to remove bones — and the first item on the altar's equipment list is the bucket for carrying out what is left after the fire.

  • v8 "hollow, of boards" — nevuv luchot. The altar of the whole sanctuary is a bronze-plated wooden box with nothing inside it. And the word for the boards is luchot, the same noun as the tablets of stone Moses is on the mountain to collect (24:12). The two objects the chapter's vocabulary links are the empty altar and the written law.

  • v8 "as He showed you on the mountain" — the fourth time in three chapters that the instruction ends by pointing back at something Moses was shown (25:9, 25:40, 26:30, and here). Nothing in Exodus describes what he saw. The pattern is invoked four times and never once depicted.

  • vv9–18 the sanctuary sits inside a fence — a hundred cubits by fifty, five cubits high, of plain white linen. Everything gold and blue and crimson is inside it; from outside, the entire structure is a long white wall a little taller than a man, with nothing visible over the top.

  • v16 "the gate of the court" — twenty cubits of blue, purple and crimson, in three hundred cubits of undyed linen. It is the only color anywhere on the outside, and it marks the one way in. The same embroiderer's work covers the door of the tent (26:36), so a person walking inward passes three colored screens, each finer than the last, and never sees a plain door.

  • v17, 19 the metals are graded by distance — gold for everything inside the veil, gold and silver at the frames, silver bands and bronze sockets around the court, bronze for the altar, bronze for every peg in the ground. The further from the ark, the cheaper the metal, with no verse saying so. The scheme is only visible if you read the inventory as a map.

  • v18 "fifty by fifty" — the court has just been given as a hundred long and fifty wide, and then the summary says the width is fifty by fifty. The phrase does not fit the measurements above it, and the Hebrew as it stands cannot be made to. It is one of the places where the building specification does not add up.

  • v20 "clear oil of beaten olives" — zakh katit: olives crushed rather than pressed, which yields the first and cleanest oil and very little of it. The lamp in front of God is fuelled by the most wasteful grade available.

  • v21 "in the tent of meeting" — ohel mo'ed, and this is its first appearance in the Bible. The structure has been the mishkan, the dwelling, and the ohel, the tent; now it gets the name it will carry through the rest of the Torah, built on mo'ed, an appointed meeting — the same root as I will meet with you there at 25:22. And the first duty attached to it is keeping a light burning from evening until morning: the one thing that must never stop is required only at night.

chapters.title: For Glory and for Beauty
chapters.html:
Exodus 28

The Ephod

1"And you — bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, from among the sons of Israel, to serve Me as priests: Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons.

2And you shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.

3And you shall speak to all the wise of heart, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, and they shall make Aaron's garments to set him apart, to serve Me as priest.

4And these are the garments they shall make: a breastpiece and an ephod and a robe, a checkered tunic, a turban and a sash. And they shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and for his sons, to serve Me as priests.

5And they shall take the gold and the blue and the purple and the crimson and the fine linen.

6And they shall make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, crimson and fine twisted linen, the work of a designer.

7It shall have two shoulder pieces joined at its two ends, and so it shall be joined together.

8And the woven band of its ephod, which is on it, shall be of the same work and of one piece with it: gold, blue, purple, crimson and fine twisted linen.

9And you shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel —

10six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the remaining six on the second stone, in the order of their birth.

11The work of a stone-cutter, engravings of a seal, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel. Set in gold settings you shall make them.

12And you shall put the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel. And Aaron shall carry their names before the LORD on his two shoulders, as a remembrance.

13And you shall make settings of gold,

14and two chains of pure gold — twisted like cords you shall make them — and you shall fasten the corded chains to the settings.

The Breastpiece

15And you shall make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a designer. Like the work of the ephod you shall make it: of gold, blue, purple, crimson and fine twisted linen you shall make it.

16Square it shall be, folded double, a span its length and a span its width.

17And you shall set in it a setting of stones, four rows of stones. A row of carnelian, topaz and emerald — the first row.

18And the second row: turquoise, sapphire and diamond.

19And the third row: jacinth, agate and amethyst.

20And the fourth row: beryl, onyx and jasper. They shall be set in gold in their settings.

21And the stones shall be according to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names — engravings of a seal, each with its name, for the twelve tribes.

22And you shall make on the breastpiece chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.

23And you shall make on the breastpiece two rings of gold, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.

24And you shall put the two gold cords on the two rings, at the ends of the breastpiece.

25And the two ends of the two cords you shall put on the two settings, and put them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, toward its front.

26And you shall make two rings of gold and set them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on its edge that faces the ephod, inward.

27And you shall make two rings of gold and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, low down, at the front, close to its seam, above the woven band of the ephod.

28And they shall bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue, so that it rests on the woven band of the ephod, and the breastpiece will not come loose from the ephod.

29And Aaron shall carry the names of the sons of Israel on the breastpiece of judgment, on his heart, when he goes into the holy place, as a remembrance before the LORD always.

30And you shall put into the breastpiece of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be on Aaron's heart when he goes in before the LORD. And Aaron shall carry the judgment of the sons of Israel on his heart before the LORD always.

The Robe

31And you shall make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue.

32And the opening for his head shall be in the middle of it. Its opening shall have a binding of woven work all around — like the opening of a coat of mail it shall be — so that it is not torn.

33And on its hem you shall make pomegranates of blue and purple and crimson, all around its hem, and bells of gold between them all around:

34a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, on the hem of the robe all around.

35And it shall be on Aaron when he serves, and its sound shall be heard when he goes into the holy place before the LORD and when he comes out — and he shall not die.

The Plate, and the Rest

36And you shall make a plate of pure gold, and engrave on it, with the engravings of a seal: Holy to the LORD.

37And you shall fasten it with a cord of blue, and it shall be on the turban — on the front of the turban it shall be.

38And it shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron shall carry the guilt of the holy things that the sons of Israel set apart, in all their holy gifts. And it shall be on his forehead always, for their acceptance before the LORD.

39And you shall weave the tunic in checker work of fine linen, and make a turban of fine linen, and a sash you shall make, the work of an embroiderer.

40And for Aaron's sons you shall make tunics, and make them sashes, and make them caps, for glory and for beauty.

41And you shall clothe Aaron your brother with them, and his sons with him, and anoint them and ordain them and set them apart, and they shall serve Me as priests.

42And make them linen undergarments to cover their naked flesh, reaching from the waist to the thighs.

43And they shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they come into the tent of meeting, or when they come near the altar to serve in the holy place, so that they do not bear guilt and die. A lasting statute for him and for his seed after him."

Notes

  • vv2, 40 "for glory and for beauty" — le-khavod u-le-tif'aret, and it is said twice: once of Aaron's garments and once of his sons'. Kavod is the heavy word — weight, wealth, honor, the glory that settles on Sinai in 24:16. The clothes are not described as functional or as protective. Their stated purpose is that the man wearing them should be weighty and beautiful to look at.

  • v3 "the wise of heart… a spirit of wisdom" — chakhmei lev, filled with ruach chokhmah. Hebrew has no separate word for technical skill: the dyers, weavers and goldsmiths who will build this are called wise, and the thing filling them is the same spirit and the same wisdom the rest of the canon uses for understanding God. Craftsmanship and wisdom are one word here, and the book does not treat that as a metaphor.

  • vv12, 29, 38 Aaron carries three things — the same verb, nasa, to lift and bear, three times in one chapter, and each time on a different part of his body. The names of the tribes go on his shoulders (v12). The judgment of the tribes goes on his heart (v30). The guilt of their holy things goes on his forehead (v38). Nothing in the chapter says this is a pattern. The verb says it.

  • v15 "a breastpiece of judgment" — choshen mishpat, the same mishpat as the rulings of chapter 21 and the specification of the tabernacle in 26:30. What hangs on the high priest's chest is named for a legal decision, and v30 makes that explicit: he carries the judgment of the sons of Israel on his heart.

  • vv17–20 twelve stones, and most of the names are unrecoverable — the Hebrew lists odem, pitdah, bareqet, nofekh, sappir, yahalom, leshem, shevo, achlamah, tarshish, shoham, yashfeh. A few are reasonably secure; several are pure guesswork, and English Bibles disagree with each other row by row. Sappir is most likely lapis lazuli rather than the modern sapphire. What is certain is the arrangement: four rows of three, one per tribe, each cut with a name.

  • v30 "the Urim and the Thummim" — left untranslated, because nobody knows what they were. The words look like plurals of ur, light, and tam, whole or complete, so lights and perfections is a fair guess at the letters and no help at all with the objects. They are introduced here with no description, no instruction for making them, and no explanation — the one item in the entire sanctuary the text does not tell Moses how to build.

  • vv33–35 bells on the hem — gold bells alternating with woven pomegranates, and the reason given is not decoration: its sound shall be heard when he goes in… and he shall not die. The holiest man in Israel is fitted with a noise-maker so that his entering can be heard, and the alternative named is his death. Nothing says who is listening.

  • v32 "like the opening of a coat of mail" — ke-fi tachra, and tachra occurs in the Bible only here and in the matching verse at 39:23. A garment of some kind, reinforced at the neck; armor is the traditional guess from the context and cannot be confirmed. The instruction attached to it is clear enough: the collar is to be bound so that it cannot tear.

  • v36 "a plate of pure gold… Holy to the LORD" — tzitz, a word that elsewhere means a blossom or a shining thing. Two words are cut into it, qodesh la-YHWH, and they sit on the forehead of a man who is at that moment carrying the guilt of everything the nation has dedicated. The label and the load are on the same square inch.

  • v41 "and ordain them" — the Hebrew is u-milleta et yadam, and you shall fill their hand. It is the fixed idiom for installing a priest, used through the Torah, and what the hand is filled with is never stated in the phrase itself — chapter 29 will put portions of the ordination ram into their palms. English "ordain" comes by way of the Latin; the Hebrew describes a gesture.

  • v42 "linen undergarments to cover their naked flesh" — and this is the answer to 20:26, eight chapters earlier: you shall not go up by steps onto My altar, so that your nakedness is not uncovered on it. The problem raised at the very first altar law is solved here by tailoring. It is the last item in a chapter about glory and beauty, and it is underwear.

And it shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron shall carry the guilt of the holy things that the sons of Israel set apart, in all their holy gifts. And it shall be on his forehead always, for their acceptance before the LORD.
And you shall weave the tunic in checker work of fine linen, and make a turban of fine linen, and a sash you shall make, the work of an embroiderer.
And for Aaron's sons you shall make tunics, and make them sashes, and make them caps, for glory and for beauty.
And you shall clothe Aaron your brother with them, and his sons with him, and anoint them and ordain them and set them apart, and they shall serve Me as priests.
And make them linen undergarments to cover their naked flesh, reaching from the waist to the thighs.

And they shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they come into the tent of meeting, or when they come near the altar to serve in the holy place, so that they do not bear guilt and die. A lasting statute for him and for his seed after him."

chapters.title: Filling Their Hands
chapters.html:
Exodus 29

Washing and Clothing

1"And this is the thing you shall do for them, to set them apart to serve Me as priests. Take one bull of the herd and two rams, unblemished,

2and unleavened bread, and unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil. Of fine wheat flour you shall make them.

3And you shall put them in one basket and bring them near in the basket — along with the bull and the two rams.

4And Aaron and his sons you shall bring near to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and wash them with water.

5And you shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic and the robe of the ephod and the ephod and the breastpiece, and fasten the ephod on him with its woven band.

6And you shall set the turban on his head, and put the holy crown on the turban.

7And you shall take the anointing oil and pour it on his head, and anoint him.

8And his sons you shall bring near, and clothe them with tunics.

9And you shall gird them with sashes — Aaron and his sons — and bind caps on them. And the priesthood shall be theirs by a lasting statute. And you shall fill the hand of Aaron and the hand of his sons.

The Bull and the Two Rams

10And you shall bring the bull near before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lean their hands on the bull's head.

11And you shall slaughter the bull before the LORD, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

12And you shall take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and all the rest of the blood you shall pour out at the base of the altar.

13And you shall take all the fat that covers the innards, and the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, and turn them to smoke on the altar.

14And the flesh of the bull and its hide and its dung you shall burn in fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.

15And you shall take the one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lean their hands on the ram's head.

16And you shall slaughter the ram, and take its blood and throw it against the altar all around.

17And the ram you shall cut into its pieces, and wash its innards and its legs, and put them with its pieces and with its head.

18And you shall turn the whole ram to smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a quieting smell, an offering by fire to the LORD.

19And you shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lean their hands on the ram's head.

20And you shall slaughter the ram, and take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear and on the lobe of the right ear of his sons, and on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot. And you shall throw the blood against the altar all around.

21And you shall take some of the blood that is on the altar, and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and on his garments, and on his sons and on his sons' garments with him. And he shall be holy, and his garments, and his sons and his sons' garments with him.

What Fills the Hand

22And you shall take from the ram the fat, and the fat tail, and the fat that covers the innards, and the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, and the right thigh — for it is a ram of ordination —

23and one round loaf of bread, and one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer, from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.

24And you shall put all of it on Aaron's palms and on the palms of his sons, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.

25And you shall take them from their hands and turn them to smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering, as a quieting smell before the LORD. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.

26And you shall take the breast of the ram of Aaron's ordination, and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD. And it shall be your portion.

27And you shall make holy the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution — what was waved and what was lifted — from the ram of ordination, from what is Aaron's and from what is his sons'.

28And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons as a lasting due from the sons of Israel, because it is a contribution. And it shall be a contribution from the sons of Israel, out of their peace offerings — their contribution to the LORD.

29And the holy garments of Aaron shall belong to his sons after him, to be anointed in them and to have their hands filled in them.

30Seven days shall the priest who succeeds him from among his sons wear them, the one who comes into the tent of meeting to serve in the holy place.

31And the ram of ordination you shall take, and boil its flesh in a holy place.

32And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the bread that is in the basket, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

33And they shall eat the things by which atonement was made, to fill their hands, to set them apart. And an outsider shall not eat, because they are holy.

34And if any of the flesh of the ordination, or of the bread, is left until morning, then you shall burn what is left in fire. It shall not be eaten, because it is holy.

35And you shall do for Aaron and for his sons in this way, according to all that I have commanded you. Seven days you shall fill their hands.

36And a bull as a sin offering you shall make each day for atonement, and you shall purge the altar by making atonement on it, and anoint it to set it apart.

37Seven days you shall make atonement on the altar and set it apart, and the altar shall be most holy. Whatever touches the altar shall become holy.

The Continual Offering

38And this is what you shall offer on the altar: two lambs a year old, day by day, continually.

39The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer between the evenings.

40And a tenth of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil, and a drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine, for the one lamb.

41And the second lamb you shall offer between the evenings. Like the grain offering of the morning and like its drink offering you shall do for it, as a quieting smell, an offering by fire to the LORD.

42A continual burnt offering for your generations, at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD — where I will meet with you, to speak to you there.

43And I will meet there with the sons of Israel, and it shall be made holy by My glory.

44And I will set apart the tent of meeting and the altar, and Aaron and his sons I will set apart, to serve Me as priests.

45And I will dwell among the sons of Israel, and I will be their God.

46And they shall know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt to dwell among them. I am the LORD their God."

Notes

  • vv9, 29, 33, 35 "fill the hand" — mille yad, four times in this chapter, and 28:41 made it the word for ordaining a priest. Here the chapter finally says what the hand is filled with: in v24 the fat, the tail, the liver, the kidneys, the right thigh and three kinds of bread are all piled onto Aaron's palms, and he holds them out. The ram itself is eil ha-millu'im, the ram of fillings. English "ordain" is an abstraction; the Hebrew is a man standing with his arms full.

  • v1 "unblemished" — temimim, the plural of tam. The word Genesis uses for Noah (6:9), commands to Abraham (17:1), and calls Jacob (25:27), and the word Exodus 26:24 uses for two boards meeting flush. A moral description, a carpentry term and a livestock grade are one word, and the animal sense is the concrete one the others are built on.

  • vv10, 15, 19 "lean their hands on the head" — samakh, and it is not a light touch: the verb is used for leaning your weight on something, propping a thing up so it does not fall. Three times, before each killing, the men who are being ordained put their weight on the animal's skull. The text never says what the gesture means.

  • v20 "the lobe of the right ear… the thumb… the big toe" — blood is put at three points, and they are the ends of the body: the part that hears, the part that works, the part that walks. Nothing in the chapter comments on the choice. The word for the ear lobe, tenukh, occurs in only two rites in the Torah: this ordination, carried out in Leviticus 8, and the cleansing of someone healed of a skin disease (Leviticus 14:14). Making a priest and readmitting an outcast are marked on the body the same way.

  • vv18, 25, 41 "a quieting smell" — reach nichoach, from nuach, to rest — the root behind Noah's name, the ark coming to rest, and the dove finding nowhere to set her foot. English prints a pleasing aroma, which is the sense and not the word. The smoke settles something. Its first appearance in this canon is Genesis 8:21, where God smells it after the flood and promises never again.

  • vv24, 27 "waved… lifted" — two motions with two nouns. Tenufah is from nuf, to swing or wave; terumah is from rum, to lift, the same word as the contribution that funded the sanctuary in 25:2. One portion is swung, one is raised, and the two together are what the priests get to keep. The gestures are named more precisely than the theology behind them.

  • v34 "burn what is left in fire" — the leftovers of an ordination meal cannot be saved, and the reason given is that they are holy, not that they would spoil. Holiness in this system is a property that makes food dangerous rather than valuable, and the same rule governs the manna in chapter 16, which bred worms if kept overnight.

  • v37 "whatever touches the altar shall become holy" — holiness here behaves like a charge that transfers on contact. Nothing says this is desirable. The chapter that ends by ordering underwear to protect priests from dying (28:42–43) treats the altar as something that makes whatever brushes it no longer ordinary.

  • vv38–42 "continually… between the evenings" — two lambs a day forever, one at dawn and one bein ha-arbayim, between the two evenings, a phrase the Hebrew never defines and Jewish practice has argued over since. The sanctuary's basic rhythm is not festivals or pilgrimages: it is two animals a day, every day, marking the ends of the daylight.

  • vv45–46 "to dwell among them" — the last two verses answer the whole question. Shakhan, the verb behind mishkan, twice: I will dwell among the sons of Israel, and then, as the stated reason for the exodus itself, who brought them out of the land of Egypt to dwell among them. Four chapters of joinery, cloth and blood, and the purpose given at the end is residence. The point of getting them out of Egypt was to move in.

chapters.title: A Ransom for His Life
chapters.html:
Exodus 30

The Altar of Incense

1"And you shall make an altar for burning incense. Of acacia wood you shall make it.

2A cubit its length and a cubit its width — square it shall be — and two cubits its height. Its horns shall be of one piece with it.

3And you shall overlay it with pure gold: its top and its sides all around, and its horns. And you shall make for it a molding of gold all around.

4And two rings of gold you shall make for it, beneath its molding, on its two sides — you shall make them on its two flanks — as holders for the poles to carry it with.

5And you shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

6And you shall set it in front of the veil that is by the ark of the Testimony, in front of the cover that is over the Testimony, where I will meet with you.

7And Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on it. Morning by morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.

8And when Aaron sets up the lamps between the evenings, he shall burn it — incense continually before the LORD, for your generations.

9You shall not offer on it strange incense, or a burnt offering, or a grain offering; and you shall not pour a drink offering on it.

10And Aaron shall make atonement on its horns once a year. With the blood of the sin offering of atonement, once a year, he shall make atonement on it, for your generations. It is most holy to the LORD."

A Ransom for His Life

11And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

12"When you take a head count of the sons of Israel, to number them, then each shall give a ransom for his life to the LORD when they are numbered — so there will be no plague among them when they are numbered.

13This they shall give, everyone who passes over to those counted: half a shekel by the shekel of the sanctuary — the shekel is twenty gerahs — half a shekel as a contribution to the LORD.

14Everyone who passes over to those counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the contribution of the LORD.

15The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than the half shekel, when giving the contribution of the LORD to make atonement for your lives.

16And you shall take the atonement silver from the sons of Israel and give it for the service of the tent of meeting. And it shall be a remembrance for the sons of Israel before the LORD, to make atonement for your lives."

The Basin

17And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

18"And you shall make a basin of bronze, and its stand of bronze, for washing. And you shall set it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water there.

19And Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet from it.

20When they come into the tent of meeting they shall wash with water, and they shall not die — or when they come near the altar to serve, to turn an offering by fire into smoke for the LORD.

21And they shall wash their hands and their feet, and they shall not die. And it shall be a lasting statute for them, for him and for his seed, through their generations."

The Anointing Oil

22And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

23"And you — take for yourself the finest spices: five hundred of liquid myrrh, and half as much fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty, and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane,

24and five hundred of cassia, by the shekel of the sanctuary, and a hin of olive oil.

25And you shall make of it a holy anointing oil, a blended compound, the work of a perfumer. A holy anointing oil it shall be.

26And with it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the Testimony,

27and the table and all its vessels, and the lampstand and its vessels, and the altar of incense,

28and the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and the basin and its stand.

29And you shall set them apart, and they shall be most holy. Whatever touches them shall become holy.

30And Aaron and his sons you shall anoint, and set them apart to serve Me as priests.

31And to the sons of Israel you shall say: 'This shall be a holy anointing oil to Me through your generations.

32On a person's flesh it shall not be poured, and you shall not make any like it in its proportions. It is holy; holy it shall be to you.

33Anyone who blends any like it, or who puts any of it on an outsider, shall be cut off from his people.'"

The Incense

34And the LORD said to Moses, "Take for yourself spices — stacte and onycha and galbanum — spices, and pure frankincense. Each shall be in equal measure.

35And you shall make of it incense, a compound, the work of a perfumer, salted, pure, holy.

36And you shall grind some of it fine, and put some of it before the Testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.

37And the incense you make — you shall not make any in its proportions for yourselves. It shall be holy to you for the LORD.

38Anyone who makes any like it, to smell it, shall be cut off from his people."

Notes

  • v9 "strange incense" — qetoret zarah, and the adjective is the one that comes back to kill. In Leviticus 10:1 the two men named first in 28:1 as the sons being ordained — Nadab and Abihu — take their fire pans, put incense on them, and bring near before the LORD esh zarah, strange fire, which He had not commanded. Same word, same altar, two chapters after they are dressed for the job. The prohibition is written here, in a verse about equipment, before either of them has done anything.

  • vv7–8 "morning by morning… between the evenings" — the incense is tied to the lamps: it is burned when Aaron trims them at dawn and when he lights them at dusk. It is not a separate rite with its own hours. Twice a day someone crosses the room to do the wicks, and the smoke goes up while he is in there anyway.

  • v12 "when you take a head count" — ki tissa et rosh, literally when you lift the head of the sons of Israel, which is the ordinary Hebrew for taking a census. And the law attached to it is startling: each man must pay kofer nafsho, a ransom for his life, so there will be no plague among them when they are numbered. Counting people is treated as dangerous in itself, and the danger is stated without explanation. The tax is not a fee for the count; it is protection from it.

  • v15 "the rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less" — the ransom is a flat half shekel and it is forbidden to pay differently in either direction. A wealthy man may not buy a larger share of the atonement, and a poor man's is not smaller. It is the one payment in the Torah where the amount is fixed against the payer's means in both directions.

  • v16 "the atonement silver… for the service of the tent" — the money does not disappear into a treasury. It is spent on the building, and 38:27 will account for it: the silver sockets the whole frame stands in are cast from this. The tabernacle's foundations are the ransom money of the men who were counted.

  • vv20–21 "and they shall not die" — said twice in two verses, about washing hands and feet. The same sentence closed chapter 28 about the linen undergarments. Three times now the instruction for a garment or a basin ends by naming the alternative, and the alternative is always death. Nothing in these chapters treats proximity to the sanctuary as safe.

  • vv23–25, 34–35 two recipes, given in full — the anointing oil and the incense are the only formulas in the Torah written out with quantities: myrrh, cinnamon, fragrant cane, cassia and olive oil for the one; stacte, onycha, galbanum and frankincense for the other. Several of the ingredients cannot be identified with confidence — shecheleth, onycha, is usually taken as the operculum of a sea snail, and nataf, stacte, means only a drop. The proportions are exact and the substances are half-unknown.

  • vv32–33, 37–38 the recipes are capital secrets — both close the same way: make any in these proportions for yourself, and you are cut off from your people. And v38 names the offense precisely — anyone who makes any like it to smell it. Not to sell, not to worship with: to enjoy. The penalty attaches to private pleasure in a smell.

  • v25 "the work of a perfumer" — ma'aseh roqeach, the same construction as the designer and the embroiderer in chapter 26. The sanctuary's trades are named one by one: weaver, designer, embroiderer, stone-cutter, goldsmith, perfumer. Every one of them is called wise in 28:3.

  • v35 "salted" — memullach, from melach, salt. What a salted incense is, nobody can say: proposals run from literally salted, to well-mixed, to seasoned in the sense of blended, and the Hebrew gives no help. It sits in a list of three adjectives — salted, pure, holy — where the other two are plain.

And the incense you make — you shall not make any in its proportions for yourselves. It shall be holy to you for the LORD.
Anyone who makes any like it, to smell it, shall be cut off from his people."

chapters.title: In the Shadow of God
chapters.html:
Exodus 31

Bezalel and Oholiab

1And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.

3And I have filled him with the spirit of God — with wisdom and with understanding and with knowledge and with every kind of craft —

4to devise designs, to work in gold and in silver and in bronze,

5and in the cutting of stones for setting, and in the carving of wood, to work in every kind of craft.

6And I — here, I have given him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan. And in the heart of everyone wise of heart I have put wisdom, and they shall make everything I have commanded you:

7the tent of meeting, and the ark for the Testimony, and the cover that is on it, and all the vessels of the tent;

8and the table and its vessels, and the pure lampstand and all its vessels, and the altar of incense;

9and the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and the basin and its stand;

10and the woven garments, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons' garments, for serving as priests;

11and the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense for the holy place. According to all that I have commanded you, they shall do."

The Sign

12And the LORD said to Moses, saying,

13"And you — speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'Above all, you shall keep My sabbaths. For it is a sign between Me and you, through your generations, so that you may know that I am the LORD who sets you apart.

14And you shall keep the sabbath, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall surely be put to death, for anyone who does work on it — that soul shall be cut off from among his people.

15Six days work shall be done, and on the seventh day is a sabbath of solemn rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does work on the sabbath day shall surely be put to death.

16And the sons of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to make the sabbath through their generations — an everlasting covenant.

17Between Me and the sons of Israel it is a sign forever. For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day He stopped, and He took breath.'"

Written by the Finger of God

18And when He had finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, He gave Moses the two tablets of the Testimony — tablets of stone, written by the finger of God.

Notes

  • v2 "Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur" — Betzal'el is a sentence: be-tzel El, in the shadow of God. In a country where shade is what keeps a man alive, being in someone's shadow is being under their protection. And his grandfather is named: Hur is the man who held up one of Moses' arms at Rephidim while Aaron held the other (17:12), and who was left holding the court with Aaron when Moses went up the mountain (24:14). The builder of the sanctuary is the grandson of the man who kept Moses' hands steady.

  • v3 "filled him with the spirit of God" — ruach Elohim, and this is what it is given for: gold, silver, bronze, stonecutting and joinery. The list that follows the spirit is a list of trades. Compare 28:3, where the weavers are filled with a spirit of wisdom — in this book, the only people said to be filled with a spirit are craftsmen.

  • v4 "to devise designs" — lachshov machashavot, the verb with its own noun. The root is chashav, to think, calculate, reckon — the same root behind ma'aseh choshev, the work of a designer, on the inner curtains and the veil (26:1, 26:31), and behind the choshen, the breastpiece. The Hebrew for artistic design is a word for thinking hard.

  • v6 "Oholiab… of the tribe of Dan" — the second craftsman is paired deliberately with the first, and the pairing is unbalanced. Bezalel is of Judah, the tribe that gets the kingship. Oholiab is of Dan, the tribe descended from Bilhah, Rachel's servant girl (Genesis 30:6) — the one Genesis 49 compares to a snake in the road. The two men who build the sanctuary come from the top and the bottom of the family.

  • v6 "in the heart of everyone wise of heart I have put wisdom" — the sentence doubles back on itself: wisdom is put into those who are already wise. It is not a promise to make the unskilled able. The gift goes to people who could already do the work, and the text does not explain the difference between what they had and what was added.

  • vv12–17 the sabbath lands here, and the placement is the point — six chapters of instructions for building, and the last word before the tablets are handed over is: not on the seventh day. The command is attached to the construction project, not to worship or to rest in general. Whatever else this sanctuary is worth, it is not worth working through a sabbath to finish it.

  • v13 "a sign" — ot, the same noun as the rainbow after the flood (Genesis 9:12) and circumcision in the flesh (Genesis 17:11). The previous two signs were a thing in the sky and a mark on the body. This one is a day — a sign made out of time rather than matter, and the only one of the three that has to be renewed every week.

  • v15 "a sabbath of solemn rest" — shabbat shabbaton, the noun doubled on itself, which is how Hebrew makes a superlative: a sabbath of sabbaths, the same construction as qodesh ha-qodashim, holy of holies. English has to reach for an adjective the Hebrew does not use.

  • v17 "He stopped, and He took breath" — shavat va-yinnafash. The first verb is the one the noun shabbat is made from: to stop, to cease, not to sleep. The second is built on nefesh, throat and breath and life — the verb used at 23:12 for what the ox, the donkey and the foreigner get to do on the seventh day. It is said here of God. The same word for the animal catching its breath and for the Creator catching His.

  • v18 "written by the finger of God" — ketuvim be-etzba Elohim. The phrase appeared once before in this book, in Pharaoh's court, when the magicians could not reproduce the gnats and said this is the finger of God (8:19). The first time it was an argument they lost; here it is a description of handwriting. And the next sentence in the book is the people at the bottom of the mountain telling Aaron to make them gods.

chapters.title: These Are Your Gods
chapters.html:
Exodus 32

The Calf

1And the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, and the people gathered against Aaron and said to him, "Rise, make us gods who will go before us — because this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him."

2And Aaron said to them, "Tear off the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters, and bring them to me."

3And all the people tore off the gold rings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.

4And he took them from their hand and shaped it with an engraving tool, and made it into a molten calf. And they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."

5And Aaron saw, and built an altar in front of it. And Aaron called out and said, "A festival to the LORD tomorrow."

6And they rose early the next day and offered burnt offerings and brought peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

Leave Me Alone

7And the LORD said to Moses, "Go, get down — because your people, whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, have ruined themselves.

8They have turned aside quickly from the way I commanded them. They have made themselves a molten calf and bowed down to it and sacrificed to it, and said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'"

9And the LORD said to Moses, "I have seen this people, and here — it is a stiff-necked people.

10And now, leave Me alone, and My anger will burn against them, and I will finish them. And I will make you into a great nation."

11And Moses pleaded with the LORD his God and said, "Why, LORD, should Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a strong hand?

12Why should Egypt say, 'With evil intent He brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to finish them off the face of the ground'? Turn from Your burning anger and relent of the evil against Your people.

13Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel Your servants, to whom You swore by Yourself and said to them, 'I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your seed, and they shall inherit it forever.'"

14And the LORD relented of the evil He had said He would do to His people.

Down the Mountain

15And Moses turned and went down from the mountain, and the two tablets of the Testimony were in his hand — tablets written on both their sides, on one side and on the other they were written.

16And the tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, cut into the tablets.

17And Joshua heard the sound of the people as they shouted, and he said to Moses, "There is a sound of war in the camp."

18And he said, "It is not the sound of shouting for victory, and it is not the sound of shouting for defeat. A sound of singing is what I hear."

19And it came to pass, when he came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, that Moses' anger burned, and he threw the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.

20And he took the calf they had made and burned it in the fire, and ground it until it was powder, and scattered it on the face of the water, and made the sons of Israel drink it.

21And Moses said to Aaron, "What did this people do to you, that you brought such a great sin on them?"

22And Aaron said, "Let my lord's anger not burn. You yourself know the people, that they are set on evil.

23And they said to me, 'Make us gods who will go before us — because this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.'

24And I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, tear it off.' And they gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf."

Who Is for the LORD

25And Moses saw the people, that they were let loose — for Aaron had let them loose, to the derision of those who rose against them.

26And Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, "Whoever is for the LORD — to me!" And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.

27And he said to them, "This is what the LORD, God of Israel, has said: Each man put his sword on his thigh. Pass back and forth from gate to gate in the camp, and each man kill his brother and each man his companion and each man his neighbor."

28And the sons of Levi did according to Moses' word, and about three thousand men of the people fell that day.

29And Moses said, "Fill your hands today for the LORD — for each man has gone against his son and against his brother — and so bring a blessing on yourselves today."

Blot Me Out

30And it came to pass the next day that Moses said to the people, "You yourselves have sinned a great sin. And now I will go up to the LORD. Perhaps I can make atonement for your sin."

31And Moses returned to the LORD and said, "Please — this people has sinned a great sin, and they have made themselves gods of gold.

32And now, if You would forgive their sin — and if not, blot me out, please, from Your book that You have written."

33And the LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against Me, him I will blot out of My book.

34And now, go, lead the people to where I told you. Here — My messenger will go before you. And on the day I call to account, I will call them to account for their sin."

35And the LORD struck the people because they made the calf — the one Aaron made.

Notes

  • v1 "this Moses, the man" — zeh Mosheh ha-ish, and the demonstrative does the work: not Moses, but this Moses fellow. In the same breath they say he is the one who brought us up from the land of Egypt, crediting the man rather than God — and in v4 they will say the calf did it, in exactly the same words. The subject changes twice in four verses and the sentence does not.

  • v2 "the gold rings that are in the ears" — nizmei ha-zahav, and nezem is the ring Abraham's servant put in Rebekah's nose in Genesis 24:47. The last time gold jewelry came off Egyptians it was plunder carried out at the exodus (12:35). It goes back into the fire here.

  • v4 "These are your gods, Israel" — elleh elohekha, plural verb and plural pronoun, for one calf. Elohim is grammatically plural and normally takes singular verbs when it means God; here the verb is plural too, so the sentence commits: these brought you up. The people in v1 asked for gods who will go — also plural — while looking at one animal.

  • vv4, 24 Aaron tells it twice, and the second version is a lie — v4: he took them from their hand and shaped it with an engraving tool, and made it into a molten calf. Two deliberate acts with a tool. v24, to Moses: I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf. The narrator has already told the reader what happened, so the reader watches the high priest of Israel claim the thing made itself. And v35, the last line of the chapter, quietly settles it: the calf — the one Aaron made.

  • v6 "rose up to play" — le-tzacheq, the verb built on Isaac's name. Genesis used it for whatever Ishmael was doing in 21:9, for Isaac and Rebekah in 26:8, and for what Potiphar's wife accused Joseph of in 39:14. Its range runs from laughing to mocking to sexual play, and this verse gives no context at all — the same refusal to specify as Genesis 21:9. Whatever it means here, the word is a grandson's name.

  • v9 "stiff-necked" — qesheh oref, hard of neck, and this is its first appearance in the Bible. The noun is the back of the neck, and its last use was nine chapters earlier in a promise: I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you (23:27), literally give them to you by the neck. The part of the body that means an enemy in flight now means this people facing God.

  • v10 "leave Me alone… I will make you into a great nation" — hanichah li. God asks Moses to let go of Him, which concedes that Moses is holding on, and then offers him Abraham's promise — I will make of you a great nation is word for word what was said at Genesis 12:2. Moses is offered the founding of a new chosen people and spends the next three verses arguing him out of it, using Abraham as the argument.

  • vv12, 14 "relent" — nacham, the root behind Noah's name and behind Genesis 6:6, where the LORD regretted that He had made man. Moses asks God to be sorry about the evil, and v14 says He was. English "relent" and "repent" both reach for it; the Hebrew word is the one for a change of feeling, and this chapter has it happen to God twice at a man's request.

  • v18 the sound is described three times — ein qol anot gevurah, ve-ein qol anot chalushah, qol annot anokhi shomea. The same verb anah three times, and it is a word that means both to answer and to sing: no sound of answering-in-strength, no sound of answering-in-weakness, a sound of singing. Joshua the soldier hears a battle. Moses, who has just been told what is down there, hears a choir.

  • v20 "made the sons of Israel drink it" — burned, ground to powder, scattered on water, drunk. Four verbs to destroy an object that could simply have been melted down. The one ritual in the Torah that makes a person drink something is the ordeal of a wife suspected of unfaithfulness (Numbers 5), where the water carries a written curse dissolved into it.

  • v29 "Fill your hands today" — mil'u yedkhem, the exact idiom for ordaining a priest, used four times in chapter 29 and translated there as ordain. Levi is installed into the priesthood in this verse, and the qualification is the killing just described. The tribe that gets the sanctuary is ordained with swords, on the day the sanctuary's first object was melted down and drunk.

  • v32 "blot me out from Your book" — the first mention in the Bible of a book God keeps with names in it, and it appears in an unfinished sentence: if You would forgive their sin — and then nothing, no main clause, the offer breaking off before it is made. Moses cannot say forgive them, only start to. What he can finish is the alternative, and it is that his own name be erased.
