chapters.title: Show Me Your Glory
chapters.html:
Exodus 33

The Ornaments

1And the LORD said to Moses, "Go, go up from here — you and the people you brought up from the land of Egypt — to the land I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, 'To your seed I will give it.'

2And I will send a messenger before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite —

3to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up among you, because you are a stiff-necked people, or I would finish you on the way."

4And the people heard this bad word and they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.

5And the LORD said to Moses, "Say to the sons of Israel: You are a stiff-necked people. If I went up among you for one moment, I would finish you. And now, take your ornaments off yourself, and I will know what to do with you."

6And the sons of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments, from Mount Horeb onward.

The Tent Outside the Camp

7And Moses would take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far off from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. And everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting, which was outside the camp.

8And it would be, when Moses went out to the tent, that all the people would rise and stand, each at the entrance of his own tent, and watch Moses until he went into the tent.

9And it would be, when Moses went into the tent, that the pillar of cloud came down and stood at the entrance of the tent, and He spoke with Moses.

10And all the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, and all the people would rise and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.

11And the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his companion. And he would return to the camp — but his attendant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, would not move out of the tent.

If Your Face Does Not Go

12And Moses said to the LORD, "See — You say to me, 'Bring this people up,' and You have not let me know whom You will send with me. And You Yourself said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favor in My eyes.'

13And now, if I have found favor in Your eyes, let me know Your ways, so that I may know You and find favor in Your eyes. And see, this nation is Your people."

14And He said, "My face will go, and I will give you rest."

15And he said to Him, "If Your face is not going, do not bring us up from here.

16For how will it be known that I have found favor in Your eyes, I and Your people, if not by Your going with us — so that we are marked out, I and Your people, from every people on the face of the ground?"

17And the LORD said to Moses, "This thing you have spoken, I will also do, because you have found favor in My eyes, and I know you by name."

The Cleft of the Rock

18And he said, "Show me, please, Your glory."

19And He said, "I Myself will make all My goodness pass before your face, and I will call out the name of the LORD before you. And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion."

20And He said, "You cannot see My face, because no human being can see Me and live."

21And the LORD said, "Here is a place beside Me, and you shall stand on the rock.

22And it will be, when My glory passes by, that I will put you in the cleft of the rock and cover you with My palm until I have passed by.

23And I will take away My palm, and you will see My back. But My face will not be seen."

Notes

  • v3 "I will not go up among you" — the offer is the land without the giver. Everything promised to Abraham is still on the table — the country, the driving out of the nations, the milk and honey — and the one thing withdrawn is God's own company. And the reason given is not punishment but danger: or I would finish you on the way. He is saying that traveling with them would kill them.

  • vv4–6 "his ornaments" — edyo, the jewelry that in 32:2 came off their ears and went into the fire. What is left of it comes off again here, and this time it is not melted down, it is simply not worn. The chapter's first act after the calf is a nation taking off its gold and leaving it off, "from Mount Horeb onward."

  • v7 "he called it the tent of meeting" — ohel mo'ed, the name given to the tabernacle at 27:21. But the tabernacle has not been built; chapters 35–40 are still to come. This is a different tent, Moses' own, pitched deliberately outside the camp. So the book has two structures with one name, and the one that exists at this moment is the one God will not come into the camp to occupy.

  • v11 "face to face" — panim el panim, and nine verses later: you cannot see My face, because no human being can see Me and live (v20). The chapter states both, in the same conversation, without a word of reconciliation. The plainest reading is that face to face is the Hebrew for speaking directly, the way a man speaks to his companion — which the verse itself supplies as the comparison — while v20 is about seeing. Whether that settles it is a question the text leaves open, and this rendering leaves it open too.

  • v11 "Joshua… would not move out of the tent" — a single clause, dropped in without comment. Moses goes back to the camp each time. The young man stays. Nothing is made of it here, and the book never explains what he was doing in there.

  • v14 "My face will go" — panai yelekhu. English Bibles print "My presence will go," which is the sense and hides the word: the whole argument from v11 to v23 is conducted in the noun panim, face. God's face will go; Moses says if Your face does not go, do not move us; and the argument ends with God covering Moses with His hand so that His face is not seen. One word, eight times, holding the chapter together.

  • v16 "so that we are marked out" — ve-niflinu, from pala, the root behind wonder and miracle — to be separated off, made distinct, set apart as remarkable. Moses' argument is that there is no observable difference between Israel and anyone else except that God travels with them. Not the law, not the land, not the ancestry: the company.

  • v19 "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious" — ve-channoti et asher achon, the same construction as ehyeh asher ehyeh, I will be what I will be, at the burning bush (3:14). Hebrew builds these by repeating a verb around its own relative clause, and what they do is refuse to specify. Asked to show His glory, God answers with a sentence shaped exactly like the one He gave when asked His name.

  • v20 "no human being can see Me and live" — lo yir'ani ha-adam va-chai. And nine chapters back, seventy-four elders saw the God of Israel and ate and drank (24:10–11). The book records both and never addresses the gap.

  • vv22–23 "the cleft of the rock… you will see My back" — achorai, the back parts, what is behind. The arrangement is physical and almost domestic: a place to stand, a crack in a rock, a hand over the man's face until the moment has gone by, then the hand lifted and one look at what is already leaving. What Moses asked for was kavod, the weight and glory. What he is given is the sight of it from behind, after it has passed.

speech.text: Exodus 33
The Ornaments

And the LORD said to Moses, "Go, go up from here — you and the people you brought up from the land of Egypt — to the land I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, 'To your seed I will give it.'
And I will send a messenger before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite —
to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up among you, because you are a stiff-necked people, or I would finish you on the way."
And the people heard this bad word and they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.

And the LORD said to Moses, "Say to the sons of Israel: You are a stiff-necked people. If I went up among you for one moment, I would finish you. And now, take your ornaments off yourself, and I will know what to do with you."
And the sons of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments, from Mount Horeb onward.
The Tent Outside the Camp

And Moses would take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far off from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. And everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting, which was outside the camp.
And it would be, when Moses went out to the tent, that all the people would rise and stand, each at the entrance of his own tent, and watch Moses until he went into the tent.
And it would be, when Moses went into the tent, that the pillar of cloud came down and stood at the entrance of the tent, and He spoke with Moses.
And all the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, and all the people would rise and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.
And the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his companion. And he would return to the camp — but his attendant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, would not move out of the tent.
If Your Face Does Not Go

And Moses said to the LORD, "See — You say to me, 'Bring this people up,' and You have not let me know whom You will send with me. And You Yourself said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favor in My eyes.'
And now, if I have found favor in Your eyes, let me know Your ways, so that I may know You and find favor in Your eyes. And see, this nation is Your people."
And He said, "My face will go, and I will give you rest."
And he said to Him, "If Your face is not going, do not bring us up from here.

For how will it be known that I have found favor in Your eyes, I and Your people, if not by Your going with us — so that we are marked out, I and Your people, from every people on the face of the ground?"
And the LORD said to Moses, "This thing you have spoken, I will also do, because you have found favor in My eyes, and I know you by name."
The Cleft of the Rock
And he said, "Show me, please, Your glory."

And He said, "I Myself will make all My goodness pass before your face, and I will call out the name of the LORD before you. And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion."
And He said, "You cannot see My face, because no human being can see Me and live."
And the LORD said, "Here is a place beside Me, and you shall stand on the rock.
And it will be, when My glory passes by, that I will put you in the cleft of the rock and cover you with My palm until I have passed by.
And I will take away My palm, and you will see My back. But My face will not be seen."

chapters.title: The Skin of His Face
chapters.html:
Exodus 34

The Second Tablets

1And the LORD said to Moses, "Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered.

2And be ready in the morning, and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and stand there for Me on the top of the mountain.

3And no one shall come up with you, and no one shall be seen anywhere on the mountain; and the flocks and the herds shall not graze in front of that mountain."

4And he cut two tablets of stone like the first ones. And Moses rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, and took the two tablets of stone in his hand.

5And the LORD came down in the cloud and stood with him there, and called out the name of the LORD.

6And the LORD passed before his face and called out: "The LORD, the LORD — God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love and truth,

7keeping loyal love for thousands, carrying guilt and rebellion and sin — and not leaving it unpunished, calling the guilt of fathers to account on sons and on sons' sons, on the third and on the fourth generation."

8And Moses hurried and bowed to the ground and knelt.

9And he said, "If now I have found favor in Your eyes, my Lord, let my Lord go among us — because it is a stiff-necked people — and forgive our guilt and our sin, and take us as Your own."

The Words of the Covenant

10And He said, "Here — I am cutting a covenant. In front of all your people I will do wonders that have not been created in all the earth or in any nation. And all the people among whom you are will see the work of the LORD, because it is a fearful thing that I am doing with you.

11Keep what I am commanding you today. Here — I am driving out from before you the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.

12Watch yourself, or you will cut a covenant with the inhabitants of the land you are coming into, and it will become a snare among you.

13You shall tear down their altars and shatter their standing stones and cut down their sacred poles.

14For you shall not bow down to another god — because the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

15Or you will cut a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they will whore after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, and one will invite you and you will eat of his sacrifice.

16And you will take some of his daughters for your sons, and his daughters will whore after their gods and make your sons whore after their gods.

17You shall not make molten gods for yourself.

18The Festival of Unleavened Bread you shall keep. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time of the month of Abib, because in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.

19Everything that first opens the womb is Mine, and all your livestock that bears a male — the firstling of ox and sheep.

20And the firstling of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem. And they shall not appear before My face empty-handed.

21Six days you shall work, and on the seventh day you shall stop. In plowing and in harvest you shall stop.

22And the Festival of Weeks you shall make for yourself, the firstfruits of the wheat harvest; and the Festival of the Gathering at the turn of the year.

23Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the face of the Lord, the LORD, God of Israel.

24For I will dispossess nations before you and widen your border, and no one will covet your land when you go up to appear before the face of the LORD your God three times in the year.

25You shall not slaughter the blood of My sacrifice with anything leavened, and the sacrifice of the festival of Passover shall not stay the night until morning.

26The first of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring to the house of the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.

27And the LORD said to Moses, "Write down these words — because by these words I have cut a covenant with you and with Israel."

28And he was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten words.

The Skin of His Face

29And it came to pass, when Moses came down from Mount Sinai — and the two tablets of the Testimony were in Moses' hand as he came down from the mountain — that Moses did not know that the skin of his face had grown horns from speaking with Him.

30And Aaron and all the sons of Israel saw Moses, and here — the skin of his face had grown horns. And they were afraid to come near him.

31And Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the assembly came back to him, and Moses spoke to them.

32And afterward all the sons of Israel came near, and he commanded them everything the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.

33And Moses finished speaking with them, and he put a veil over his face.

34And when Moses came in before the LORD to speak with Him, he would take the veil off until he came out. And he would come out and tell the sons of Israel what he had been commanded.

35And the sons of Israel would see Moses' face, that the skin of Moses' face had grown horns. And Moses would put the veil back over his face until he came in to speak with Him.

Notes

  • v1 "Cut for yourself two tablets" — the first set were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God (32:16). This time the stone is Moses' own work; he quarries and shapes them and carries them up. The replacement covenant is written on material a man made.

  • v6 "slow to anger" — erekh appayim, literally long of nostrils. In Hebrew anger lives in the nose: charah af, the burning of the nostril, is what happens to Moses in 32:19 and to God throughout. A long nose is one that takes a long time to flare. The English idiom is a temperature; the Hebrew is a distance.

  • vv6–7 the formula, and the sentence that breaks it — this list of thirteen words is quoted back at God across the rest of the Hebrew Bible more than any other sentence in the Torah. And it does not end where a reader expects. Carrying guilt and rebellion and sin — the verb is nasa, the load verb Aaron carries guilt with in 28:38 — and then immediately: ve-naqqeh lo yenaqqeh, and clearing, He will not clear. The two halves are not reconciled. Mercy is stated in the fullest terms available and then, in the same breath, limited, and the text offers no formula for how both hold.

  • v9 Moses turns the reason inside out — in 33:3 God gave the refusal and its grounds: I will not go up among you, because you are a stiff-necked people. Here Moses asks for the opposite using the identical clause: let my Lord go among us — because it is a stiff-necked people. Same three words, same causal particle, reversed. What God gave as a reason to stay away, Moses gives as the reason to come.

  • v10 "wonders" — nifla'ot, from pala, the root Moses used one chapter earlier when he said that God going with them is what would make Israel marked out from every people (33:16). The answer to that argument is given in the same root: distinctness was the request, and wonders are what is promised.

  • v13 "their sacred poles" — asherim, wooden objects standing for the goddess Asherah, and the Hebrew names her. English Bibles print "groves" (following the Greek and the Latin) or "Asherah poles"; what the word is, exactly — a living tree, a carved pole, an image — the text never describes.

  • vv19–20 the redemption clause is here — at 22:29 the law said flatly the firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me with nothing about buying them back. Here the same law is given with the clause attached: a donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken, and every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem. The book carries both versions and this is the one with a way out.

  • v21 "In plowing and in harvest you shall stop" — the sabbath law is given a second time with one clause added, and it names the two weeks of the year when stopping costs most. A farmer can rest in a slack season without it meaning anything. The verse specifies the days when it does.

  • vv27–28 who wrote the second tablets — v1 has God say I will write on the tablets. v27 has God tell Moses write down these words. Then v28: and he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten words, with no subject named. The Hebrew leaves it open, and the two instructions in the same chapter point different ways. This rendering keeps the pronoun as the Hebrew has it.

  • vv29, 30, 35 "the skin of his face had grown horns" — qaran or panav, and the verb is built on qeren, horn. It is used of an animal's horns everywhere else in the Bible; this is the only place it is a verb, and the only place it is said of a face. Light radiating in beams is the reading behind "shone," and it is a guess from the shape of a horn rather than from any other use of the word. The Latin translated it cornuta, horned, which is why Michelangelo's Moses has horns. The Hebrew says horn and says nothing else.

  • vv33–35 the veil — masveh, a noun that occurs in the Bible only in these three verses. And the sequence is the reverse of what a reader expects: he takes it off to speak with God and puts it on to speak with Israel. Paul reads the passage this way in Greek — not like Moses, who put a covering over his face so that the sons of Israel would not look at the end of what was fading (2 Corinthians 3:13) — but Exodus never says the shining faded, and never says why the veil was worn.

chapters.title: What the People Brought
chapters.html:
Exodus 35

The Sabbath, Before Anything Is Built

1And Moses assembled all the assembly of the sons of Israel and said to them, "These are the words that the LORD has commanded, to do them.

2Six days work shall be done, and on the seventh day there shall be a holy thing for you — a sabbath of solemn rest for the LORD. Anyone who does work on it shall be put to death.

3You shall not kindle a fire in any of your settlements on the sabbath day."

The Call for the Contribution

4And Moses said to all the assembly of the sons of Israel, "This is the thing that the LORD has commanded, saying:

5Take from among you a contribution for the LORD. Everyone of a willing heart shall bring it — the LORD's contribution: gold and silver and bronze,

6and blue and purple and crimson, and fine linen and goats' hair,

7and rams' skins dyed red, and fine leather, and acacia wood,

8and oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense,

9and onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.

10And everyone with a wise heart among you shall come and make everything that the LORD has commanded:

11the dwelling, its tent and its covering, its clasps and its frames, its bars, its pillars and its sockets;

12the ark and its poles, the cover, and the veil of the screen;

13the table and its poles and all its vessels, and the bread of the Presence;

14and the lampstand for the light and its vessels and its lamps, and the oil for the light;

15and the altar of incense and its poles, and the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the dwelling;

16the altar of burnt offering and the bronze grating that belongs to it, its poles and all its vessels; the basin and its stand;

17the hangings of the court, its pillars and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court;

18the pegs of the dwelling and the pegs of the court and their cords;

19the finely worked garments for serving in the holy place — the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, for serving as priests."

They Bring More Than Is Asked

20And all the assembly of the sons of Israel went out from before Moses.

21And everyone whose heart lifted him came, and everyone whose spirit moved him, and they brought the LORD's contribution for the work of the tent of meeting and for all its service and for the holy garments.

22And they came, the men along with the women. Everyone of a willing heart brought brooches and rings and signet rings and pendants, every article of gold — everyone who presented an offering of gold to the LORD.

23And everyone who had with him blue and purple and crimson, and fine linen and goats' hair, and rams' skins dyed red and fine leather, brought them.

24Everyone setting aside a contribution of silver or bronze brought the LORD's contribution, and everyone who had acacia wood with him for any of the work of the service brought it.

25And every woman with a wise heart spun with her own hands, and they brought what they had spun: the blue and the purple, the crimson and the fine linen.

26And all the women whose heart lifted them, in wisdom, spun the goats' hair.

27And the leaders brought the onyx stones and the stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece,

28and the spice and the oil for the light and for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense.

29Every man and woman whose heart moved them to bring for all the work that the LORD had commanded to be done through Moses — the sons of Israel brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.

The Two Men Who Will Build It

30And Moses said to the sons of Israel, "See — the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,

31and has filled him with the spirit of God — with wisdom and with understanding and with knowledge and with every kind of craft —

32to devise designs, to work in gold and in silver and in bronze,

33and in the cutting of stones for setting, and in the carving of wood, to work in every kind of craft of design.

34And He has put it in his heart to teach — him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

35He has filled them with a wise heart to do all the work of a craftsman and a designer and an embroiderer in blue and in purple, in crimson and in fine linen, and of a weaver — doers of every kind of work and devisers of designs."

Notes

  • vv1–3 the sabbath comes first, and it is the fence around the whole project — the instructions in chapters 25–31 ended with the sabbath law (31:12–17); the building account here begins with it. The command to build is wrapped in it on both sides. And the one activity singled out, you shall not kindle a fire, is the one this particular work cannot proceed without — there is no casting of gold, no smelting of silver, no bronze grating without a fire. The prohibition names the craft that is about to start.

  • v3 "in any of your settlements" — moshevoteikhem, from yashav, to sit or dwell. It is the same root as mishkan only by accident of subject matter, not of word: the dwelling God occupies is mishkan, from shakhan, to settle in or tent among. Two different verbs for dwelling run through these chapters, and English has one word for both.

  • vv5, 21, 24 "contribution" — terumah, from rum, to be high, with the causative sense to lift something up and set it apart. It is not a tax and not a gift in the ordinary sense: the noun names the act of raising a portion out of a larger quantity and putting it beyond ordinary use. What is being described three times in this chapter is people separating their own metal from the rest of what they own.

  • v10 "everyone with a wise heart" — chakham lev, and chokhmah is the word for wisdom throughout the Hebrew Bible — Solomon's wisdom, the wisdom of Proverbs. Here it means knowing how to cut a stone, weave a fabric, cast a socket. The language makes no distinction at all between the wisdom of a sage and the skill of a metalworker; both are chokhmah, and in this chapter only craftsmen have it. The same phrase is used of the women who spin in v25 and of Bezalel and Oholiab in v35.

  • v19 "the finely worked garments" — bigdei ha-serad, and serad occurs four times in the Hebrew Bible, all four in Exodus and all four in this same phrase (31:10, here, 39:1, 39:41). Nothing else in the language constrains it. It has been read as woven, plaited, finely worked, and as a term for the coverings the furniture was wrapped in for transport. The word cannot be recovered; what it attaches to is clear.

  • vv21, 26 "whose heart lifted him" — nesa'o libbo, the heart as the thing that picks a person up and carries him. The verb is nasa, the load verb: what Aaron does with the guilt of Israel in 28:38, what God does with guilt and rebellion and sin in 34:7. English says moved, which is a nudge. Hebrew says his heart took his weight.

  • v22 "brooches and rings and signet rings and pendants" — four words for jewelry and two of them are guesses. Chach is a hook or clasp elsewhere in the Bible, including the hook put in a captive's jaw; nezem is a ring worn in the nose or the ear — it is the word for the ring Abraham's servant gives Rebekah; tabba'at is a signet ring. Kumaz occurs twice in the whole Bible, here and at Numbers 31:50, in both places in a list of gold ornaments, and it has never been identified.

  • v22 the gold that went the other way — this is the second time in six chapters that Israel takes off its gold jewelry and hands it over. In 32:2–3 Aaron says tear off the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters and they do it, and it becomes the calf. The same nezem, the same voluntary stripping, the same metal. Nothing in the text remarks on it.

  • v25 "spun with her own hands" — the only place in the Torah where women are named as the makers of something in the sanctuary, and it is stated twice, in two different registers: the ones with a wise heart spin the dyed yarn and the linen, and the ones whose heart lifts them spin the goats' hair, which is the coarse outer covering. Both groups get the vocabulary of wisdom that Bezalel gets in v31.

  • v32 "to devise designs" — lachshov machashavot, the verb with its own noun. Chashav is to think, calculate, reckon, plan; machashavah is a thought or a plan, and it is the word used of what humanity's heart produces before the flood — every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil, all day long (Genesis 6:5). The word for the imagination that brought the flood is the word for the imagination that furnishes the sanctuary, and it is the highest praise the chapter gives.

He has filled them with a wise heart to do all the work of a craftsman and a designer and an embroiderer in blue and in purple, in crimson and in fine linen, and of a weaver — doers of every kind of work and devisers of designs."

chapters.title: Enough, and More Than Enough
chapters.html:
Exodus 36

The Only Time Israel Has to Be Told to Stop

1"And Bezalel and Oholiab shall work, and every man with a wise heart in whom the LORD has put wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work of the service of the holy place, according to all that the LORD has commanded."

2And Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every man with a wise heart in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom — everyone whose heart lifted him to come near to the work, to do it.

3And they took from before Moses the whole contribution that the sons of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the holy place, to do it. And the people kept bringing him freewill offerings, morning after morning.

4And all the wise men doing all the work of the holy place came, each from the work he was doing,

5and said to Moses, "The people are bringing far more than the service needs for the work that the LORD commanded to be done."

6And Moses gave an order, and they had word carried through the camp: "Let no man or woman do any more work for the contribution of the holy place." And the people were held back from bringing,

7and what had come in was enough for all the work, to do it — and there was more than enough.

The Curtains and the Tent

8And every one with a wise heart among those doing the work made the dwelling of ten curtains of fine twisted linen, and blue and purple and crimson. With cherubim, the work of a designer, he made them.

9The length of one curtain, twenty-eight cubits, and the width four cubits, for one curtain. One measure for all the curtains.

10And he joined five of the curtains to one another, and five curtains he joined to one another.

11And he made loops of blue on the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set; he did the same on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.

12Fifty loops he made on the one curtain, and fifty loops he made on the edge of the curtain that is in the second set, the loops facing one another.

13And he made fifty clasps of gold and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, and the dwelling was one.

14And he made curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the dwelling. Eleven curtains he made them.

15The length of one curtain, thirty cubits, and four cubits the width of one curtain. One measure for the eleven curtains.

16And he joined five of the curtains by themselves, and six of the curtains by themselves.

17And he made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain in the first set, and fifty loops he made on the edge of the curtain of the second set.

18And he made fifty clasps of bronze to join the tent together, to be one.

19And he made a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above it.

The Frames

20And he made the frames for the dwelling of acacia wood, standing upright.

21Ten cubits the length of a frame, and a cubit and a half the width of one frame.

22Two tenons for each frame, fitted to one another. So he did for all the frames of the dwelling.

23And he made the frames for the dwelling: twenty frames for the south side, facing south.

24And forty sockets of silver he made under the twenty frames — two sockets under one frame for its two tenons, and two sockets under the next frame for its two tenons.

25And for the second side of the dwelling, on the north side, he made twenty frames,

26and their forty sockets of silver — two sockets under one frame and two sockets under the next frame.

27And for the rear of the dwelling, toward the sea, he made six frames.

28And two frames he made for the corners of the dwelling, at the rear.

29And they were doubled below, and together they were whole to the top of each, at the first ring. So he did for both of them, for the two corners.

30And there were eight frames, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets — two sockets, two sockets, under each frame.

31And he made bars of acacia wood: five for the frames of the one side of the dwelling,

32and five bars for the frames of the second side of the dwelling, and five bars for the frames of the dwelling at the rear, toward the sea.

33And he made the middle bar to run through the middle of the frames from end to end.

34And he overlaid the frames with gold, and made their rings of gold as holders for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.

The Veil and the Screen

35And he made the veil of blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen. The work of a designer he made it, with cherubim.

36And he made for it four pillars of acacia and overlaid them with gold, their hooks of gold, and cast for them four sockets of silver.

37And he made a screen for the entrance of the tent, of blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer,

38and its five pillars and their hooks; and he overlaid their tops and their bands with gold, and their five sockets were bronze.

Notes

  • vv5–7 the one place in the Bible where giving has to be stopped — the craftsmen walk off the job to report a problem, and the problem is that too much is coming in. Moses issues the only order of its kind in the Torah: let no man or woman do any more work for the contribution. Six chapters earlier the same people handed over the same gold as fast as it was asked for, and Aaron cast it into a calf (32:3–4). Nothing here points back at that. The book simply puts the two scenes in the same building and lets a reader notice that the fault was never the generosity.

  • v6 "they had word carried through the camp" — va-ya'aviru qol, literally they made a voice pass over. The verb is avar, the crossing-over verb: what the LORD does through Egypt on the night of the Passover (12:12), what Israel does through the sea. Here it is what a proclamation does through a camp — the announcement travels the way a person travels, from one end to the other.

  • v7 "and there was more than enough" — ve-hoter, one word, from yatar, to remain over. It is the surplus word: what is left of the Passover lamb in the morning (12:10), what the hail has left for the locusts to eat (10:15). The building account of the sanctuary ends its collection with the same word the plague narrative used for leftovers, and it is the only time in Exodus the leftover is a good thing.

  • vv8–38 every command has become a past tense — chapter 26 gave all of this in the second person future: you shall make ten curtains, you shall make fifty clasps of gold. Here every one of those sentences returns as va-ya'as, and he made. Thirty verses of instruction are repeated almost word for word with only the verb changed, and the repetition is the point — Hebrew narrative reports obedience by saying the command again with the tense moved. Nothing is summarized; the reader is made to walk the whole list twice.

  • v8 "the work of a designer" and v37 "the work of an embroiderer" — ma'aseh choshev and ma'aseh roqem, two distinct crafts, and the text assigns them by rank of location. The designer's work — from chashav, to devise or calculate — goes on the ten curtains and on the veil that hides the ark (v35). The embroiderer's work goes on the screen at the outer entrance (v37). The nearer a fabric gets to the ark, the higher the craft named on it.

  • v25 "the second side of the dwelling" — tsela, and the noun is rib. It is the word for what is taken out of the man in Genesis 2:21–22 — He took one of his ribs… and the LORD God built the rib that He had taken from the man into a woman. Hebrew uses it for the flank of a building as naturally as for the flank of a body, and the verb attached to it in Genesis is banah, to build. The dwelling has ribs and sides; the first woman is constructed out of one.

  • vv27, 32 "toward the sea" — yammah, from yam, sea. Hebrew has no neutral word for west: west is where the Mediterranean is. The other directions in these verses work the same way — negev for south is the name of the dry country below Judah, and teimanah is the right hand of someone facing the sunrise. A Hebrew compass is a description of standing in one specific place and looking east.

  • v29 "they were whole to the top of each" — tammim, from tamam, to be complete or without defect. It is the word for Noah, tamim in his generations (Genesis 6:9), and the standard for an animal fit to be offered. Applied here to two corner planks, it means they ran the full height without a break — the same word for a man's integrity, a lamb's soundness, and a joint that does not gap.

chapters.title: What Bezalel Made
chapters.html:
Exodus 37

The Ark

1And Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood — two and a half cubits its length, and a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height.

2And he overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold on it all around.

3And he cast for it four rings of gold on its four feet — two rings on its one side and two rings on its other side.

4And he made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

5And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark.

6And he made a cover of pure gold — two and a half cubits its length and a cubit and a half its width.

7And he made two cherubim of gold. Hammered work he made them, at the two ends of the cover:

8one cherub at the end on this side and one cherub at the end on that side. Out of the cover itself he made the cherubim, at its two ends.

9And the cherubim were spreading their wings upward, covering the cover with their wings, their faces each toward his brother. Toward the cover were the faces of the cherubim.

The Table

10And he made the table of acacia wood — two cubits its length and a cubit its width and a cubit and a half its height.

11And he overlaid it with pure gold and made a molding of gold for it all around.

12And he made for it a rim a handbreadth wide all around, and made a molding of gold for its rim all around.

13And he cast for it four rings of gold and put the rings on the four corners that belong to its four legs.

14Close to the rim were the rings, holders for the poles, to carry the table.

15And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, to carry the table.

16And he made the vessels that are on the table — its dishes and its pans and its bowls and the jars the drink offering is poured from — of pure gold.

The Lampstand

17And he made the lampstand of pure gold. Hammered work he made the lampstand — its base and its shaft; its cups, its bulbs and its blossoms were of one piece with it.

18And six branches going out from its sides — three branches of the lampstand from its one side and three branches of the lampstand from its other side.

19Three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the one branch, a bulb and a blossom; and three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the next branch, a bulb and a blossom. So for the six branches going out from the lampstand.

20And on the lampstand itself, four cups shaped like almond blossoms, its bulbs and its blossoms;

21and a bulb under the first two branches of one piece with it, and a bulb under the next two branches of one piece with it, and a bulb under the next two branches of one piece with it — for the six branches going out from it.

22Their bulbs and their branches were of one piece with it; all of it one hammered work of pure gold.

23And he made its seven lamps, and its tongs and its fire pans, of pure gold.

24Of a talent of pure gold he made it, with all its vessels.

The Altar of Incense, and the Oil

25And he made the altar of incense of acacia wood — a cubit its length and a cubit its width, square, and two cubits its height. Its horns were of one piece with it.

26And he overlaid it with pure gold — its roof and its walls all around, and its horns — and made a molding of gold for it all around.

27And two rings of gold he made for it under its molding, on its two sides, on its two flanks, as holders for poles to carry it with.

28And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

29And he made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.

Notes

  • v1 "And Bezalel made the ark" — chapter 36 reported the curtains, the frames and the veil with no one named: and every one with a wise heart among those doing the work made…, and then thirty verses of and he made, subject unstated. The ark is the one object in the sanctuary the text attaches a name to. Whoever cut the boards, this is the thing Bezalel is recorded as having made with his own hands.

  • v9 "their faces each toward his brother" — ish el achiv, a man toward his brother. Biblical Hebrew has no word for each other; it borrows the language of kinship and uses it for objects — planks fitted to one another (26:3), curtains facing one another, and here two gold figures turned face to face. The reciprocal is always built out of a relationship word, so the grammar of two things facing is the grammar of two brothers.

  • vv19–20 "cups shaped like almond blossoms" — meshuqqadim, from shaqed, the almond. The almond is the first tree in the land to flower, weeks ahead of anything else, and its name is spelled with the same consonants as shoqed, watching, staying awake. Jeremiah is shown a branch of an almond, and the answer is I am watching over My word to do it (Jeremiah 1:11–12) — the whole exchange is that one pair of words. The lampstand that stands burning in the dark of the sanctuary is shaped, four times over, into the tree whose name means staying awake.

  • v24 "of a talent of pure gold" — kikkar, and the word means a round flat disc: a loaf of bread, a district of flat country. It is what Lot looks out over in Genesis 13:10, the whole kikkar of the Jordan — the Round, the plain. Weight got its name from the shape the metal was cast in. About seventy-five pounds of gold, hammered out of one piece, with nothing joined and nothing soldered.

  • v26 "its roof and its walls" — gag and qirot, the ordinary words for the roof and the walls of a house. The incense altar is eighteen inches square and three feet high, and the Hebrew describes it in the vocabulary of architecture, as though it were a building rather than a piece of furniture. Its four raised corners are qarnot, horns, which is the animal word. A small house with horns, standing in front of the veil.

  • v29 "the work of a perfumer" — ma'aseh roqeach, and it is the last craft named in the chapter and the only one that is not carpentry, metalwork or weaving. Everything else in the sanctuary is shaped by hand; the oil and the incense are compounded. 30:32–33 makes the recipe itself restricted — anyone who mixes it to the same formula for ordinary use is cut off from his people. It is the one object in the tent that can be copied exactly, which is why it is the one the law has to forbid copying.

chapters.title: The Court, and the Reckoning of the Metal
chapters.html:
Exodus 38

The Altar and the Basin

1And he made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood — five cubits its length and five cubits its width, square, and three cubits its height.

2And he made its horns on its four corners; its horns were of one piece with it. And he overlaid it with bronze.

3And he made all the vessels of the altar — the pots and the shovels and the basins, the forks and the fire pans. All its vessels he made of bronze.

4And he made for the altar a grating, a network of bronze, under its ledge below, reaching halfway up.

5And he cast four rings at the four ends of the bronze grating, as holders for the poles.

6And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.

7And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it with them. Hollow, of boards, he made it.

8And he made the basin of bronze and its stand of bronze — out of the mirrors of the women who served in ranks at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

The Court

9And he made the court. For the south side, facing south, the hangings of the court of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits;

10their pillars twenty and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands, silver.

11And for the north side, a hundred cubits; their pillars twenty and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands, silver.

12And for the side toward the sea, hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars ten and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars and their bands, silver.

13And for the front side, toward the sunrise, fifty cubits.

14Hangings of fifteen cubits for the one shoulder; their pillars three and their sockets three.

15And for the second shoulder — on this side of the gate of the court and on that — hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three and their sockets three.

16All the hangings of the court all around were of fine twisted linen.

17And the sockets for the pillars were bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands, silver, and the overlay of their tops, silver; and they were banded with silver, all the pillars of the court.

18And the screen of the gate of the court was the work of an embroiderer — blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen — twenty cubits long, and its height, along its width, five cubits, matching the hangings of the court.

19And their pillars four and their sockets four, of bronze; their hooks silver, and the overlay of their tops and their bands, silver.

20And all the pegs for the dwelling and for the court all around were bronze.

The Reckoning

21These are the accounts of the dwelling, the dwelling of the Testimony, which were counted at Moses' mouth — the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

22And Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything that the LORD commanded Moses;

23and with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan — a craftsman and a designer, and an embroiderer in blue and in purple and in crimson and in fine linen.

24All the gold used for the work, in all the work of the holy place — the gold of the offering was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, by the shekel of the holy place.

25And the silver of those counted in the assembly: a hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels, by the shekel of the holy place —

26a beka a head, half a shekel by the shekel of the holy place, for everyone who crossed over to those counted, from twenty years old and upward: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men.

27And the hundred talents of silver were for casting the sockets of the holy place and the sockets of the veil — a hundred sockets for the hundred talents, a talent to a socket.

28And of the thousand seven hundred and seventy-five he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their tops, and banded them.

29And the bronze of the offering was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.

30And with it he made the sockets for the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the bronze altar and the bronze grating that belongs to it, and all the vessels of the altar,

31and the sockets of the court all around and the sockets of the gate of the court, and all the pegs of the dwelling and all the pegs of the court all around.

Notes

  • v4 "under its ledge" — karkob, a word that occurs twice in the Hebrew Bible and both times of this one altar (27:5 and here). Nothing else in the language uses it, so nothing else can settle what part of the altar it names. A rim, a ledge, a projecting border partway up have all been proposed from the geometry of the verse — the grating hangs under it and reaches halfway. The shape is guessed from the measurement, not from the word.

  • v7 "Hollow, of boards, he made it" — nevuv luchot, three words, and they are the whole description of what the altar actually is. Not a block of stone and not a solid casting: a bronze-plated wooden box with nothing inside it. And luchot is the same noun as the tablets Moses carries down the mountain in 34:29. The same word for the stone God wrote on and for the planks the fire is built on.

  • v8 "out of the mirrors of the women who served in ranks" — be-mar'ot ha-tsove'ot asher tsave'u, and the verb is tsava, the word behind tseva'ot, hosts — the armies of Israel, the host of heaven, the title the LORD of hosts. It is a military word for massing and mustering, and here it is used twice in one clause of women stationed at the door of the tent. What their service was, the text does not say; the word it picks for it is the word for an army in formation. And the metal is theirs: bronze mirrors, handed over and melted, become the basin the priests wash in before they are allowed to live through the approach.

  • vv14–15 "for the one shoulder" — katef, the shoulder, used for the stretch of curtain flanking the gate. Hebrew builds architecture out of anatomy without marking it as figurative: a building has shoulders and sides, and tsela, rib, is the word for its flank (36:25). English has kept one of these — the shoulder of a road — and lost the rest.

  • v21 "the accounts… which were counted" — pequdei… asher puqqad, and paqad is one of the load-bearing verbs of the book. It is what God does at the bush and in the promise Joseph made his brothers — paqod paqadti, I have surely attended to you (3:16, and Genesis 50:24). It means to muster, to number, to call to account, to visit with attention. What is being done to this pile of metal is the same verb that is done to a nation.

  • v26 "a beka a head" — beqa la-gulgolet, and gulgolet is the skull. Hebrew counts people by skulls the way English counts cattle by head. The word traveled into Aramaic and out the other side: the place John's gospel names Golgotha is glossed there, in Greek, as the Place of a Skull (John 19:17).

  • vv25–28 the numbers check — this is the only itemized account of expenditure in the Torah, and its arithmetic closes. Six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men at half a shekel each comes to 301,775 shekels. The text says a hundred talents went into the sockets and 1,775 shekels into the hooks; subtract the hooks and 300,000 shekels are left for the hundred talents. So the chapter quietly defines its own unit: three thousand shekels to the talent, a figure stated nowhere in the Bible and recoverable only by doing the sum. And the hundred talents are spent at exactly one talent a socket — about seventy-five pounds of silver under each upright, holding up a tent.

  • v24 gold, silver, bronze, and which is which — the three metals sort themselves by distance from the ark. Gold is everything inside the veil and on it. Silver, the census money, is cast into the sockets the whole structure stands in — every man counted in Israel is, in metal, part of the foundation. Bronze is the outer court, the altar where the burning happens, and the pegs driven into the dirt. The further out a reader walks, the baser the metal gets, and the ordering is never stated; it is only ever built.

speech.text: Exodus 38
The Altar and the Basin
And he made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood — five cubits its length and five cubits its width, square, and three cubits its height.
And he made its horns on its four corners; its horns were of one piece with it. And he overlaid it with bronze.
And he made all the vessels of the altar — the pots and the shovels and the basins, the forks and the fire pans. All its vessels he made of bronze.
And he made for the altar a grating, a network of bronze, under its ledge below, reaching halfway up.
And he cast four rings at the four ends of the bronze grating, as holders for the poles.
And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it with them. Hollow, of boards, he made it.
And he made the basin of bronze and its stand of bronze — out of the mirrors of the women who served in ranks at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The Court
And he made the court. For the south side, facing south, the hangings of the court of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits;
their pillars twenty and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands, silver.
And for the north side, a hundred cubits; their pillars twenty and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands, silver.
And for the side toward the sea, hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars ten and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars and their bands, silver.
And for the front side, toward the sunrise, fifty cubits.
Hangings of fifteen cubits for the one shoulder; their pillars three and their sockets three.
And for the second shoulder — on this side of the gate of the court and on that — hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three and their sockets three.
All the hangings of the court all around were of fine twisted linen.
And the sockets for the pillars were bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands, silver, and the overlay of their tops, silver; and they were banded with silver, all the pillars of the court.

And the screen of the gate of the court was the work of an embroiderer — blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen — twenty cubits long, and its height, along its width, five cubits, matching the hangings of the court.
And their pillars four and their sockets four, of bronze; their hooks silver, and the overlay of their tops and their bands, silver.
And all the pegs for the dwelling and for the court all around were bronze.
The Reckoning
These are the accounts of the dwelling, the dwelling of the Testimony, which were counted at Moses' mouth — the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
And Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything that the LORD commanded Moses;
and with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan — a craftsman and a designer, and an embroiderer in blue and in purple and in crimson and in fine linen.
All the gold used for the work, in all the work of the holy place — the gold of the offering was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, by the shekel of the holy place.
And the silver of those counted in the assembly: a hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels, by the shekel of the holy place —

a beka a head, half a shekel by the shekel of the holy place, for everyone who crossed over to those counted, from twenty years old and upward: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men.
And the hundred talents of silver were for casting the sockets of the holy place and the sockets of the veil — a hundred sockets for the hundred talents, a talent to a socket.
And of the thousand seven hundred and seventy-five he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their tops, and banded them.
And the bronze of the offering was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
And with it he made the sockets for the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the bronze altar and the bronze grating that belongs to it, and all the vessels of the altar,
and the sockets of the court all around and the sockets of the gate of the court, and all the pegs of the dwelling and all the pegs of the court all around.

chapters.title: As the LORD Had Commanded Moses
chapters.html:
Exodus 39

The Ephod

1And from the blue and the purple and the crimson they made the finely worked garments for serving in the holy place, and they made the holy garments that were for Aaron, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

2And he made the ephod of gold, blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen.

3And they hammered out sheets of gold and cut them into threads, to work into the blue and into the purple and into the crimson and into the fine linen — the work of a designer.

4Shoulder pieces they made for it, joined together; at its two ends it was joined.

5And the woven band of its ephod, which was on it, was of one piece with it and of the same work: gold, blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

6And they made the onyx stones, set in gold settings, engraved with the engravings of a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.

7And he set them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

The Breastpiece

8And he made the breastpiece, the work of a designer, like the work of the ephod: gold, blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen.

9Square it was; they made the breastpiece folded double — a span its length and a span its width, folded double.

10And they filled it with four rows of stone. A row of carnelian, topaz and emerald — the first row.

11And the second row: turquoise, sapphire and diamond.

12And the third row: jacinth, agate and amethyst.

13And the fourth row: beryl, onyx and jasper — set in gold settings in their mountings.

14And the stones were according to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, engravings of a seal, each with its own name, for the twelve tribes.

15And they made on the breastpiece chains at the edges, of pure gold, twisted like cords.

16And they made two gold settings and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.

17And they put the two gold cords on the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.

18And the two ends of the two cords they put on the two settings, and put them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, toward its front.

19And they made two rings of gold and set them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on its edge, on the inner side facing the ephod.

20And they made two rings of gold and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, low down, at the front, close to its seam, above the woven band of the ephod.

21And they bound the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue, so that it rested on the woven band of the ephod and the breastpiece would not come loose from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

The Robe and the Rest

22And he made the robe of the ephod, the work of a weaver, entirely of blue.

23And the opening of the robe was in the middle of it, like the opening of a coat of mail, with a binding around its opening, so that it would not be torn.

24And on the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of blue and purple and crimson, twisted.

25And they made bells of pure gold and put the bells between the pomegranates on the hem of the robe all around, between the pomegranates:

26a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, on the hem of the robe all around, for serving — as the LORD had commanded Moses.

27And they made the tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver, for Aaron and for his sons,

28and the turban of fine linen, and the ornamented caps of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen,

29and the sash of fine twisted linen and blue and purple and crimson, the work of an embroiderer — as the LORD had commanded Moses.

30And they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote on it an inscription with the engravings of a seal: Holy to the LORD.

31And they put on it a cord of blue, to fasten it on the turban above, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

They Bring It All to Moses

32And all the work of the dwelling of the tent of meeting was finished. And the sons of Israel did according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses; so they did.

33And they brought the dwelling to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, its frames, its bars, and its pillars and its sockets;

34and the covering of rams' skins dyed red, and the covering of fine leather, and the veil of the screen;

35the ark of the Testimony and its poles, and the cover;

36the table, all its vessels, and the bread of the Presence;

37the pure lampstand, its lamps — the lamps set in their row — and all its vessels, and the oil for the light;

38and the gold altar, and the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;

39the bronze altar and the bronze grating that belongs to it, its poles and all its vessels; the basin and its stand;

40the hangings of the court, its pillars and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court, its cords and its pegs, and all the vessels for the service of the dwelling, for the tent of meeting;

41the finely worked garments for serving in the holy place — the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, for serving as priests.

42According to all that the LORD had commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel did all the work.

43And Moses saw all the work, and here — they had done it; as the LORD had commanded, so they had done. And Moses blessed them.

Notes

  • The sentence that will not stop — seven times — ka'asher tsivvah YHWH et Mosheh, as the LORD had commanded Moses, closes vv1, 5, 7, 21, 26, 29 and 31: seven times in thirty-one verses, once at the end of each piece of clothing. Then the chapter says it three more times in a different shape, at v32, v42 and v43. A reader in English feels a refrain. What the Hebrew is doing is closer to a legal endorsement — each item signed off as it is handed over, the way a manifest is initialled line by line.

  • vv32, 43 the end of Exodus is written in the words of the beginning of Genesis — three verbs, in the same order, with the same noun for the work. Genesis 2:2, va-yekhal Elohim… melakhto asher asah, God finished the work he had made; Exodus 39:32, va-tekhel kol avodat ha-mishkan, all the work of the dwelling was finished. Genesis 1:31, va-yar Elohim et kol asher asah ve-hinneh tov me'od, God saw all that he had made, and here — very good; Exodus 39:43, va-yar Mosheh et kol ha-melakhah ve-hinneh asu otah, Moses saw all the work, and here — they had done it. Genesis 2:3, God blessed; Exodus 39:43, Moses blessed them. A tent is finished in the vocabulary of a world being finished, and nothing in either passage points it out.

  • v3 "they hammered out sheets of gold and cut them into threads" — the only description in the Bible of how any material in the sanctuary was actually manufactured. Everywhere else the text says he made and moves on. Here it stops to explain that the gold in the cloth is real gold: beaten into foil, cut into strips, and worked in among the blue and the purple as though it were yarn. Four chapters of gold objects, and this is the one sentence about technique.

  • v23 "like the opening of a coat of mail" — ke-fi tachra, and tachra occurs twice in the Hebrew Bible, at 28:32 and here, both times in this same comparison about this same garment. Nothing else in the language defines it. Something with a reinforced neck-hole that does not tear — armor is the usual guess, and it is a guess. What the verse is certain about is the requirement: so that it would not be torn. The robe of the high priest is built to resist the one thing a man does to his clothes when someone dies.

  • vv24–26 "a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate" — the Hebrew repeats the pair rather than stating the pattern, which is how the alternation is described: not alternating, but the thing said twice so the reader walks the hem. Chapter 28 gave the reason and it is not ornament — its sound shall be heard when he goes into the holy place… and he shall not die (28:35). The most elaborate garment in the book is fitted with a noise-maker, and the alternative named is death.

  • v30 "Holy to the LORD" — qodesh la-YHWH, two words, and they are the only writing anywhere in the sanctuary. The tablets inside the ark are written, but they are shut in a box under a lid; these two words are worn on the forehead, in gold, facing out. Everything else in nine chapters of instruction is an object. This alone is a sentence.

  • v37 "the pure lampstand" — ha-menorah ha-tehorah. The adjective normally describes the gold — pure gold, a dozen times in these chapters. Here it has slid onto the lampstand itself, as though the object had taken on the quality of its metal. And nerot ha-ma'arakhah, the lamps of the row: ma'arakhah is a setting-out in order, the word used of the rows of bread on the table and of an army drawn up in line of battle.

  • v43 "And Moses blessed them" — no words are recorded. Aaron and his sons will later be handed the exact three lines to bless with, each one naming the LORD (Numbers 6:24–26); Moses here is given nothing to say. The Torah does report wordless blessings elsewhere — Jacob blesses Pharaoh twice and the text never says how (Genesis 47:7, 10) — but the occasion is unusual: almost every blessing in Genesis is spoken over someone leaving, or about what is still to come. This one is said to people who have just finished a job, about the job.

chapters.title: The Cloud Settles
chapters.html:
Exodus 40

Raise It Up

1And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"On the day of the first month, on the first of the month, you shall raise up the dwelling of the tent of meeting.

3And you shall put the ark of the Testimony there, and screen the ark with the veil.

4And you shall bring in the table and set it in order; and you shall bring in the lampstand and raise up its lamps.

5And you shall put the gold altar for incense before the ark of the Testimony, and set up the screen of the entrance to the dwelling.

6And you shall put the altar of burnt offering before the entrance of the dwelling of the tent of meeting.

7And you shall put the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water there.

8And you shall set up the court all around, and put up the screen of the gate of the court.

9And you shall take the anointing oil and anoint the dwelling and everything in it, and set it apart with all its vessels — and it shall be holy.

10And you shall anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and set the altar apart — and the altar shall be most holy.

11And you shall anoint the basin and its stand, and set it apart.

12And you shall bring Aaron and his sons near to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and wash them with water.

13And you shall clothe Aaron with the holy garments, and anoint him and set him apart, and he shall serve Me as priest.

14And his sons you shall bring near, and clothe them with tunics.

15And you shall anoint them as you anointed their father, and they shall serve Me as priests. And their anointing shall be for them a priesthood forever, through their generations."

16And Moses did according to all that the LORD commanded him; so he did.

And He Did It

17And it came to pass in the first month, in the second year, on the first of the month, that the dwelling was raised up.

18And Moses raised up the dwelling: he laid its sockets and set up its frames and put in its bars and raised up its pillars.

19And he spread the tent over the dwelling and put the covering of the tent over it, above, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

20And he took the Testimony and put it into the ark, and set the poles on the ark, and put the cover on the ark, above.

21And he brought the ark into the dwelling and set up the veil of the screen and screened the ark of the Testimony, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

22And he put the table in the tent of meeting, on the north flank of the dwelling, outside the veil.

23And he set the bread in order on it before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

24And he put the lampstand in the tent of meeting, opposite the table, on the south flank of the dwelling.

25And he raised up the lamps before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

26And he put the gold altar in the tent of meeting, before the veil,

27and burned fragrant incense on it, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

28And he set up the screen of the entrance to the dwelling.

29And the altar of burnt offering he set at the entrance of the dwelling of the tent of meeting, and offered up on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

30And he put the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water there for washing.

31And Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet from it.

32When they came into the tent of meeting and when they came near the altar, they would wash — as the LORD had commanded Moses.

33And he raised up the court all around the dwelling and the altar, and put up the screen of the gate of the court. And Moses finished the work.

The Cloud Settles

34And the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the dwelling.

35And Moses could not come into the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it and the glory of the LORD filled the dwelling.

36And whenever the cloud was lifted from over the dwelling, the sons of Israel would set out, on all their journeys.

37And if the cloud was not lifted, they would not set out, until the day it was lifted.

38For the cloud of the LORD was over the dwelling by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, on all their journeys.

Notes

  • v35 "because the cloud had settled on it" — ki shakhan alav he-anan, and shakhan is the verb the whole book has been building a noun out of. Mishkan, the dwelling, is a place of shakhan, of settling in. For sixteen chapters the word has named a thing made of boards and goat hair, and here, in the last five verses of Exodus, it finally does what its name says. And what settles is not described. Not a figure, not a voice — a cloud, and a weight called kavod, the glory, from the root meaning heavy.

  • v35 and Moses is the one left outside — at 24:18 va-yavo Mosheh be-tokh he-anan, Moses came into the middle of the cloud, and went up the mountain, and stayed forty days. Here the same cloud is twenty feet away at ground level and he cannot get in. The book that began with a man turning aside to look at a fire ends with the same man standing outside a tent he built himself, and the text offers no comment on it at all.

  • v33 "And Moses finished the work" — va-yekhal Mosheh et ha-melakhah, and the clause is Genesis 2:2 with a man's name in it: va-yekhal Elohim… melakhto asher asah, and God finished the work that he had made. Same verb, same noun, same grammar. Chapter 39 already ran the other two verbs of the creation account — God saw, God blessed; Moses saw, Moses blessed. This is the third.

  • vv4, 23 "set it in order" — ve-arakhta et erko, literally and you shall arrange its arrangement, and again at v23, va-ya'arokh alav erekh lechem, he arranged on it an arrangement of bread. Hebrew doubles a verb with its own noun to press it; English only stutters. The noun is ma'arakhah, the word for a battle line drawn up — bread laid out in rank.

  • vv22, 24 "the north flank of the dwelling" — yerekh ha-mishkan, the thigh of the dwelling. The same noun is the hip the wrestler puts out at 32:25, and the part of the body an oath about descendants is sworn on at Genesis 24:2. Hebrew gives buildings bodies without marking it as a figure of speech: the tent has a thigh, and the table stands against it.

  • v10 "most holy" — qodesh qadashim, holiness of holinesses, the construction Hebrew uses where English uses a superlative — the same shape as shir ha-shirim, song of songs, and melekh melakhim, king of kings. It is also the name of the inner room. What is being said of the altar out in the open courtyard is the grade of holiness the inmost chamber has.

  • vv2, 17 the date, and what it is two weeks short of — the first day of the first month of the second year. The first month is the one named at 12:2, this month shall be for you the head of months, and the Passover lamb was killed on its fourteenth day (12:6). So the tent goes up a fortnight before the anniversary of the night they left. The book does not say this. It just gives the date twice, once as the command and once as the fact.

  • vv36–38 Exodus ends without arriving — the last three verses are not an event but a standing arrangement: cloud by day, fire by night, and a people who move when it moves and stay when it stays. The pair goes back to 13:21, the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire that led them out of Egypt; it is the same escort, now parked on top of a tent they carry with them. The book closes with Israel still in the wilderness, camped, waiting on a cloud — and the last two words are be-khol mas'eihem, on all their journeys, plural, none of them yet made.

supplements.title: Table of Nations
supplements.html:
Table of Nations

Every people and tribe named across Genesis, Exodus, and beyond traces back through this one family. Blue is Shem's line — Abraham, Israel, and the twelve tribes. Red is Ham's line — Canaan and the peoples already living in the land. Gold-olive is Japheth's line, the most distant from Israel's own story.

Notes on what's compressed, and what's left out

Shapes. Square-cornered boxes are individual people the narrative follows. Pill shapes are peoples and nations — a name that has become a population. Dashed boxes bundle names that appear once in a genealogical list and are never seen again as characters; they are real, but the text gives them no story of their own. Each nation sits in its own pill under the person it is named for. Where Genesis 10 lists a people with no ancestor at all (the Jebusite, the Amorite), a dotted box says so rather than inventing one. A nation's own line hangs beneath its pill: the twelve tribes sit under the Israelites, and Levi's three sons under the Levites. Naphtali and Issachar read “tribe of” because Hebrew never forms an -ite name from either.

The roots under the lowest name on each branch stand for the descendants the text never counts. Every line here runs on past the last box; the chart simply stops recording.

Why Jesus hangs under Judah. Both New Testament genealogies run him through Judah — Matthew from Abraham down (1:2–16), Luke from Jesus back up (3:23–38) — and both run through Joseph, not Mary. Matthew is careful about it. Thirty-nine times the chapter says egennēsen, fathered, in an unbroken chain; at 1:16 it stops. Joseph is called the husband of Mary, and the verb flips from active to passive: of whom was born Jesus. Luke puts the same caution in four words — being son, as was supposed, of Joseph (3:23). The line on this chart is real and legal, and the text will not call it biological.

Four women, and three of them come off this chart. Matthew names women in the descent, which genealogies of the period did not usually do: Tamar (1:3), Rahab of Jericho (1:5), Ruth the Moabite (1:5, and Ruth 1:4), and at 1:6 the wife of Uriah — Uriah the Hittite (2 Samuel 11:3) — who is the only one of the four Matthew leaves unnamed. Moab is on this tree under Lot. The Hittites are on it under Heth, on Ham's side. Rahab's Jericho is Canaan. The peoples this chart spends its width separating out turn up again inside the last line on it.

Moses and Aaron are brothers. Both are sons of Amram and Jochebed, grandsons of Kohath, great-grandsons of Levi (Exodus 6:16–20), and Aaron is the elder by three years (Exodus 7:7). Miriam is their sister: the Hebrew of Exodus 6:20 names only the two brothers, but Numbers 26:59 names all three, and the Greek of Exodus 6:20 adds her there too.

Mary's own connection, as far as the text goes. Luke says Elizabeth is Mary's syngenis, her relative (1:36), and that Elizabeth is of the daughters of Aaron (1:5) — which is Levi. Luke does not say how close the relation is, and no genealogy of Mary is given anywhere. That is the whole of it; anything more precise is supplied from outside the text.

Japheth's line is thinner than the others because Genesis gives less. Seven sons (10:2), then three sons of Gomer (10:3) and four of Javan (10:4) — and there it stops. Magog, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras get no descendants at all. The summary calls them the coastlands of the nations (10:5), a maritime rather than a territorial description. Two of the names are identified in the text later: Daniel calls the Greek king the king of Javan (8:21), and pairs Madai with Persia (5:28, 9:1).

Perizzite isn't on this tree at all. Unlike Hittite, Amorite, Hivite, and Jebusite, it never appears in Genesis 10's genealogy of Canaan. Its name most likely describes a way of life — people of the open, unwalled country — rather than a bloodline, so it has no ancestor to hang from here.

This tree stops at what's directly relevant to Israel's own story. It leaves out the deeper reaches of Japheth's line, most of Genesis 36's long list of Edomite chiefs, and every genealogy past Jacob's twelve sons.

Sources: Genesis 10 (the Table of Nations), Genesis 11:10–32, 19:36–38, 22:20–24, 25:1–18, 35:22–26, 36:1–19; Exodus 3:1, 3:8, 6:16–20, 7:7; Numbers 26:59; Deuteronomy 3:9; Amos 9:7.
